## The Friend List and PlayOnline messages (2026-10-28)

- LSB's xi_profile stands in for PlayOnline (below): TLS 51220, one request per connection (hello {u32 account, the
  login's session hash}, ProfOpenData, ProfOpenAns 0x81, ProfSendReqData {kind 2, command, sub, size}, body;
  ProfRecvAns 0x83 {error, size} + body), and TLS 51240, an IRC-like session (USER, NICK U<scrambled id>, the
  profile-available notice, PING / PONG, notices as polcore base64 of a 0x48-byte header). polcore's checksum, line
  checksum and base64 (alphabet TSG8IncW..., pad T) are in net/profile.rs, checked against vectors derived from
  LSB's codec.
- Ours: net/profile.rs (requests, FriendInfo, MsgHeader, the IRC thread); MapLogin carries the account id and hash.
  client/friends.rs: in game (first zone-in) the IRC sign-on and LoadMyStatus / LoadFriendList / LoadHandleNameList /
  LoadCharacterList; ChangeMyStatus {character found, slot} once signed on and in a zone; /away /online /hide (and
  olstat) as ChangeMyStatus 1 / 0 / 4; status notices update a friend's status (Status - 1) and character, newer ages
  only; the friends' characters from xi_search wire type 1 (ID_LIST, u16 count + u32 ids, 20 a query) every 60 s
  (record and "fresh"); a dropped IRC session comes back after 30 s.
- Mail: at sign-on and on a new-message notice the mailbox (GetFileList O/m/) is downloaded (ReadFile),
  kept in <data>/mail/<account>/unread and deleted on the server (RemoveFile); read messages move to .../read. A
  friend's +0xfc bit 1 (unread mail) from the unread folder. A message's body is ours: title and text as Shift-JIS,
  each ending in NUL *(polcore's format unknown: retail clients' messages will not read right)*. Header Date = unix
  seconds *(inf)*, SenderName = our character.
- Windows (client/friendlist.rs, polmail.rs): commenu child 1 -> flistmai (commenu suspended under it, back on
  Escape); To List -> "menu    friend" (rows FUN_101eb0d0: category 4 block list, 3 pending, 2 status 4, 0 status
  1..3, else 1, by name; bars windowps 324..327 / 343, "[Hidden]" on a folded one; cells at wx + 4 + {0, 18, 138, 175,
  265}: the status icon keytops3 64 / 65 / 66 / 177 or the mail bubble 158, "(Handle)" fitted 106, "menu    contents"
  sprite 0, the character fitted 82, the zone when not ours; band windowps 75; "No friends registered." 7 0x66);
  flmes (Tell / Send Message / View Messages with FUN_101eb880's rules; the handle and its id text over them); olstat
  (marker keytops3 101 under the status in force, anc2s hand; its layout anchors it right); titlehan (our handle and id
  while the list or msglist is up; the id text is polcore's 8 base-36 digits of the nick *(inf: slot 0x1db)*).
  msglist (the windowps 275 header, From / To / type label / FUN_101c8fd0 date, unread only, by Date); a read prints
  "From: %s", "Title: %s", "Message: %s" (0x10385260..48) in mode 0x12 and opens mes2frnd (FWT) or mes1rcv; Reply,
  Accept (the "Friend's Name:" box, 9 0x22), Decline, Ignore Sender (prompt 9 0x1a, default No), Leave Unread, Exit
  (9 0x19). msgline at (16, 410), the chat line's width + 14, 15 / 300 characters; the log gives it its input row.
  One operation at a time (7 0x7a). /friendlist, /befriend (exact name, then FUN_101ffa20; ourselves or not found: 7
  0xa2; listed: 7 0xa1), the search results' Befriend (dim only on ourselves; listed: a plain message).
- Sends: request = StoreFriendList set {first free index, our list name} + WriteFile FWT "Let's be
  friends!" with the character's name, 9 0x14; accept = store + FOK, 9 0x15 (LSB clears both pending flags); decline =
  FNO, 9 0x16; reply / plain = NRM with 9 0x1f / 0x1c titles, 9 0x12 / 0x11; ignore = store set black, 9 0x18; failures
  10 0x2d / 0x6f.
- Modern: flistmai and olstat as menus in the window panel, the list and msglist as people lists with flmes /
  mes1rcv / mes2frnd beside the cursor row, msgline as a line over the chat window.
- Live (lnxtest01 = account 1000, handle "Tuxedo"; bots' accounts 1003+ played by DB rows): the loads, sign-on,
  ChangeMyStatus (in game, Away, Online); the list with Offline / Pending / the block list and the mail bubble; flmes;
  msglist; Accept (LSB cleared pending, FOK in the bot's mailbox), Ignore (block list + FNO), Reply, Decline, Exit;
  /friendlist; /befriend on ourselves (7 0xa2); both UIs. Not seen: a friend online with a character and zone (needs
  a second account signed on), the request flow on a live bot (no bot in game), netstat's mail page.
- netstat (FUN_102014f0 / FUN_10201180): page 0 the mail (windowps 2 "PlayOnline" + envelope, 418 with a system
  message; the unread count at (+0x6c, +0x10), 0x60808080) for 60 ticks (DAT_10385270), page 1 the network for 120
  (DAT_10385272), held on page 1 while nothing is unread; the modern top bar the same with its own envelope. Seen live
  in both UIs.
- Not done: netstat's Help Desk count (GM replies) and its second count (engine +0xe), the busy strip bit 0x10, deleting / unblocking / reordering
  (retail has no in-game way: the user's call), Away back to Online at login *(inf, below)*.
- Also: the K.O. windows (dead, mp_dead) drawn 8 / 4 px larger (ours, the user's call, as the raise prompt).

From the research notes:
- Profile requests (command / sub, from LSB's source): LoadHandleNameList 0x00 / 0x09, LoadCharacterList 0x01 / 0x03,
  SearchPolId 0x01 / 0x0B, LoadFriendList 0x02 / 0x03, StoreFriendList 0x02 / 0x06, ReadFile 0x03 / 0x00, WriteFile
  0x03 / 0x01, RemoveFile 0x03 / 0x02, GetFileList 0x03 / 0x03, ChangeMyStatus 0x04 / 0x05, LoadMyStatus 0x04 / 0x06.
  ProfRecvAns errors: 0 ok, 0x01 refused, 0x7E not found. A bad header, a kind other than 2 or a body of the wrong
  size or checksum gets no answer (the connection closes). LSB never checks ProfSendReqData's signature (zeros). Which
  polcore slot is which request is inferred from use.
- Checksum (polcore's sqCalcChecksum): the wrapping u32 sum of the bytes as little-endian u32 words, a 1..3-byte tail
  folded in from the top (tail = tail >> 8 | byte << 24). An IRC line is the text, 4 characters ((sum >> s) & 0x3f) +
  0x3f for s = 26, 20, 14, 8, then CR LF. The POL ids in a notice header are XORed with 0x1C273E4567891133.
- Status notice (header type 31): +0x10 connected (2, 1 profile available, 0 closed), +0x11 Status (1 offline, 2
  online, 3 away), +0x12 bit 0 playing, +0x1c where the receiver lists this friend, +0x30 u64 age in ms (a notice older
  than the last applied is dropped); then an 8-byte extension (flag 0x08: a character primitive follows, u64 charid at
  its +8).
- polcore's friend entry (300 x 0x100 at DAT_104df770 + 0xa90): +0x08 bits 13-15 the status (1..3 "Online Friends"
  with keytops3 64 / 65 / 66, 4 "Ignore List" with 177, 0 and 5..7 "Offline Friends"), bit 16 playing, bits 17-19 the
  active character slot, bit 28 pending. How polcore maps the notice's Status into it is unknown: ours Status - 1
  *(inf)*. What 3 (Busy?) and 4 are, whether the Ignore List category is ever reached, and whether the block-list
  category (windowps 343, a bar without a label) shows on retail need polcore or the original client on LSB.
- Who sees whom (LSB): A and B are visible when each lists the other (friend list, not pending) and neither blocks the
  other. A as B sees it: offline when not signed on or Invisible, else online / away; playing only while A's last
  ChangeMyStatus said in game and A has a map session (accounts_sessions). No notice for a zone, job or level change
  (xi_search has those), nor when the map session appears without a ChangeMyStatus: send it after the session exists.
- A friend playing FFXI (FUN_101eaec0; not seen live): no search record yet (+0xfc bit 0 clear) or another world: cell
  5 "<World>", kind 6 (FUN_100db7b0 gives no string, so nothing is drawn *(inf)*); else cell 5 the zone name when not
  our zone and cell 4 the character name when the record has one, kind 5 (the only kind flmes' Tell allows). Job and
  level are never shown. The list is a snapshot: only its open and a header toggle rebuild it.
- Requests on LSB: accept = store + FOK, and LSB clears pending on both rows in one transaction, then both get status
  notices; a decline (FNO) deletes the requester's pending row (by LSB's note retail keeps it pending). Every
  StoreFriendList carries the whole order tables (head 0x130: friendOrder[200], blackOrder[100], u16 count). Removing
  = StoreFriendList op 2 {Num} (the other side keeps its row and sees us offline); blocking = set {isBlack 1}. Retail
  has none of these in game: commenu's help 0xe 0x14a sends the player to the PlayOnline viewer.
- Mail engine: FFXiMain's one polcore event handler (LAB_100f28b0, slot 0x120) takes only type 0, a new message:
  FUN_100f27e0 drops duplicates, downloads it (slots 0x113 / 0x114), marks the sender's entries (+0xfc bit 1), saves it
  to local folder 7, deletes it on the server (0x118 / 0x119), counts it (engine +0xc / +0xa / +0x10 / +0x12; type 30
  SYS apart) and trims folder 7 to 200. Engine start (DAT_104df908, FUN_100f1f00): every +0xfc bit 1 cleared, folders
  7 / 8 / 6 counted (unread / read / sent *(inf)*), the server list (<= 16 headers) fetched and each queued. Types
  (header +0x3e bits 7-11): 0 NRM, 1 FWT, 3 KNK, 9 FOK, 10 FNO, 0xe..0x13 GRP, 0x1e SYS; LSB takes 0, 1, 9, 10. LSB's
  limits: 100 messages a mailbox, 10 from one sender, 50 unread sent; data <= 1024 bytes; SenderName one of the
  sender's characters; a blocked sender's message is answered ok and dropped.
- The message body (slots 0x110 encode / 0x10f decode: title <= 50, text <= 300, an attachment) is opaque to LSB; one
  message sent from the original client and read back from accounts_messages.data would settle the format. The
  handle-id text (slot 0x1db) is unknown too; titlehan draws only while polcore's mode byte *DAT_10456a28 == 0x60
  *(inf: signed on)*.
- netstat page 0: windowps 2, or 418 (red) with unread SYS, or fontshp 118 "GM"; with a GM-call count windowps 36
  "Help Desk". Page 1 is held only while there is neither mail nor a GM count. A count that grows (FUN_100f6f30, <=
  200, and FUN_100f6f00) plays SE 0039 when config 0x48 is on (default 1).
- Busy strip bit 0x10: set with DAT_10663ac8 while msglist's list job, a read (FUN_100f75f0) or a msgline send runs;
  cleared at the job's end (result 1, the engine closed, only clears it).
- Our status at login: s2c 0x00A (LAB_100facf0, LoginState @0x80 in {1, 2, 0, 6}) sets Away back to Online with a
  0x0DC clear *(inf: only the first 0x00A)*; FUN_100daf30 state 4: FUN_100f7960 re-reads and re-sends our status with
  FUN_100e46a0(1, status == Away). At character select (FUN_100ee160) retail sends ChangeMyStatus(handle, character
  index, 0, -2 keep, -1, 1).
- FUN_101ffa20(rec, flag) (/befriend flag 1, Befriend 0): key = id & 0xffff | world << 16 | (id & 0xf0000) << 8,
  SearchPolId, then our lists; result 10 (not listed) msgline mode 2; 0 with flag 1 7 0xa1, with flag 0 msgline mode 0
  (a plain message); 1 silent; else 10 0x70 "Unable to send. (%d)". Knocks (msgline modes 3 / 4: scoption child 1 with
  search flag 0x400, once per 30 s; type 3, 9 0x13) are refused by LSB.

## rem4line / rem4li2 and spoolmsg / splmsg2: the log's page overflow and Hold (2026-10-28)

- Corrects the older note under "Event text" (2019 build): rem4line is the event message's own window, open (invisible)
  for the whole message; it shows only when lines push the page off a full log.
- Records carry a print mark (+0x12): 1 the open event page (FUN_10136670 prints pages with it; each advance unmarks
  the pages before, FUN_10126a90), 2 a held chat line (FUN_101273c0, config 0x34 bit by mode: 0 say 1/9, 1 shout and
  yell 2/3/10/11, 2 tell 4/12, 3 party 5/13, 4 linkshell 6/14, 5 emote 7/15, 6 0xd2, 7 unity 0xd3/0xd4, 8 linkshell 2
  0xd5/0xd6, 9 assist J 0xdb/0xdc, 10 assist E 0xdd/0xde; our own echoes in a held channel are held too). Ours:
  ChatLog `marks`, World `page_from` / `rem_open_at`.
- Show (FUN_10162560 first loop, per printed row after the page printed): the log at its max lines, draw > 0, the row
  min(draw, max) - 1 older than the new one still the page's -> the rem shows: at the log's top-left, the log's width,
  rows x 16 + 4, its rows at (x0 + 4, y0 + 2 + 16 k), the kaipage arrow after its last row while the page waits; the
  page's rows in the log are no longer the page's (the log's own arrow, after the page's newest drawn row, goes). It
  stays until the message ends. Ours runs the test per new row of the frame (a frame's rows come together), and shows
  the current page *(inf: retail draws from its list head +0x58, stepped 4 rows by the message handler; the handler's
  double run (below) is not modelled: one page per Enter as ours always did)*.
- Spool: a held line goes into the spool (per window, of the lines it takes) with the log's period (config 0x11 x
  60 ticks); caught (+0x14a = 1) when it scrolls to or past the visible rows of a full log (walk max + 6 rows back,
  lim = vis - shown rows); the reached rows (<= 4) pinned at the log's top-left, newest at the bottom (x0 + 4, y1 - 18 +
  slide - 16 k), the frame eased +8 / -2 px a frame, 8 to slide (-4 a frame), a 20-tick fade; expired entries go, the
  newest 8 kept. Closed at the full log's open and a zone change.
- The log under them (FUN_101626e0): r = max(rem rows, spool rows) <= 4 rows off its top (the text area starts 16 r
  lower); kept open while the rem shows, the spool shows, or a waiting held line is the oldest visible row.
- Live (Lnxcsfix, a fixed 4-line log: 0x0e 1, 0x0f 4, 0x11 30): `!exec player:startEvent(60)` in Southern San
  d'Oria (Daggao's line) with a timer printing 6 system lines 7 s later: the page pinned at the top with its arrow, the
  newest 3 rows under it, gone at the message's end; with Say on Hold (0x34 1): "Bob : held" (printToPlayer type 0) and
  our held say echoes pinned while 5 pushes scrolled, gone after the 30 s period; with both, the rem drawn over the
  spool. Classic UI only: the modern chat has no such limit.
- SE 0015 (FUN_10037f50, "0015") on every Enter or click that advances a waiting page, the last too (FUN_10126880).
- Op 0xb4 sub 5 (FUN_100b0a00 case 5, byte@2: 0 on, 1 off) sets the rems' +0x60: their update (FUN_10136cd0) then
  sends message 5 every frame, each waiting page going on (SE 0015 each) until the message closes (FUN_10136ab0 clears
  it); ours event::State auto_advance. Its one site: Reisenjima (291) event_ffff @0x1f, after a 21600-tick event timer
  (subs 0xa / 0xc / 0xb). Not seen live.
- A 0x97 message's pages (op 0x48) print as mode 0xbe (asm 0x1013669b); 0x96 / 0x97 / 0x98 / 0xbe share colour id 91
  and mask bit 9, so only the record's mode differs.
- Not done: the frames' magenta tint (windowps 43, below).

From the research notes:
- The four windows (layout (16, 298) 366 x 70, one frame element): rem4line / rem4li2 (handlers DAT_105781cc /
  DAT_105781d0, owners window 1 / 2 +0x20, registry A 0x12 / B 0x0405, layer 4), spoolmsg / splmsg2 (DAT_105781d4 /
  DAT_105781d8, owners +0x1c, A 0x11 / B 0x0305, layer 3). The frame's sprite is windowps 43, a 366 x 70 newtex cell
  coloured (128, 65, 128, 169) where the log's windowps 0 is (128, 128, 128, 192): magenta and a little more
  transparent (inf: that the ref sprite's colour reaches the screen; our frame() ignores element refs; check one
  retail screenshot). Neither has A 0x40 (hidden with the UI) nor A 0x100 (closed at zone-out).
- Event message queues (FUN_10126790, DAT_104e2150 / DAT_104e2154): modes 0x96 (ops 0x1d, 0x2b, 0x49, 0xb0; s2c 0x03B,
  which LSB never sends) and 0x97 (op 0x48) are not printed but pushed to both; the push writes page 1 at once and
  opens the rem. Page flags: bit 0 waits for a key, bit 1 timed, 0x4000 drops the rem's rows at the next advance (7f
  32 / 7f 33), 0x8000 has no reader. Page 1's keyed argument is always 0 (no arrow in the rem for page 1). Each Enter
  pages both queues (FUN_10126840). FUN_10127ea0 cancels both (DAT_10488208 = 2; from the event runner, the choice
  window's close and zone-out).
- The unmark serial: FUN_10126a90 unmarks rows from entry +0x10 (record +0xc), the spool from +0x50; neither is ever
  written, so the real range is unknown (the visible result must be that earlier pages lose their mark).
- The rem's message handler FUN_10136bf0 runs FUN_10136c30 twice (asm 0x10136bff / 0x10136c1a; the 2019 build too):
  each moves +0x58 4 rows on when the list holds more than 4 and pages both queues, so one Enter on a keyed page whose
  next page is also keyed shows it and advances again (pages two at a time after page 1; a 5..8-line message ends on
  one Enter); read, not seen. Escape only while cancellable (DAT_10485a70: op 0x2e sets, 0x42 clears): SE 0003, its
  own queue cleared, DAT_10488208 = 2.
- Enter / Escape reach the rem through the generic path (FUN_1015dd00 -> FUN_10118260), blocked by placed narration
  (FUN_1015dce0) or the hidden UI; a left click (key function 0x8b released, FUN_10123a70) advances it whenever it is
  focused and the UI shown, placed narration included. While a rem is open DAT_104e1d4c +0x87 = 1: a click over no
  element plays no 0004.
- The log keeps its size (no decay, no Escape shrink) while the rem shows, or while its oldest visible row is an event
  row and such rows are no more than the rem's row count (+0x24); the same for held rows and the spool.
- Spool quirks: splmsg2's close closes spoolmsg (the full log's Enter closes spoolmsg twice and splmsg2 stays, inf);
  splmsg2 wraps at window 1's width with window 2's serials; it collects while window 2 is off and its entries just
  expire. At most 64 entries; the width is window 1's + 14 (frame element +0x22, inf); +0x5c is refreshed only at a
  reach (stale after expiries, inf).

## s2c 0x075: the border (2026-10-28)

Follows "s2c 0x075: the battlefield countdown, objective bars and text".
- FUN_10087990 on every 0x075 (our entity present): radius != 0 -> FUN_1009adb0 (FUN_10092760 drops all ten parts,
  entity +0x134 bits 9..18, then wants parts 0..7: | 0x1fe), radius 0 -> FUN_1009add0 (wants none). So any 0x075
  remakes the border, even unchanged. The entity update (FUN_1008f740's block, all.c ~112270) makes each wanted part
  with FUN_100c59b0(entity pos, entity, kind 0x35 + k), file FUN_100d43e0 = table 0x10330f34 by colour @0x25 (0x3b2,
  0x3bc) + 0xca53 = 52741 red, 52751 blue (anything over 1 counts as 0).
- The file: skeleton toum, a 208-byte mesh hf_t, idl0; schedulers init (-> efkl), pop0, lp00 (generators bou3 and
  bou2, mesh glg4 / glg3, 59 ticks), efon (op 0x73: lp00 looping), efof (op 0x2d on bou3 / bou2, op 0x5f lp00), efkl
  (op 0x1e, 0x5f). The walls are those generators on each part.
- Placement FUN_100c9c10 (asm 0x100c9c10.., the player's actor, parts at actor +0x770) each frame once all 8 parts
  are ready (vt +0x1e4), radius r > 0: d = (player - camera) with y 0, normalised; q = camera + d x render (the source
  computes |d - d| + render, so the length of d drops out); bearing deg = ftol(-atan2(q.x - cx, q.z - cz) x 57.29578);
  start = (-4 - deg / 15) x 15 (C division); part k at angle a = (start + 15 k) degrees wrapped to [-pi, pi]: position
  (cx + r sin a, the player's y, cz + r cos a), rotation (0, a, 0). near = |r - |player - c|| < render (y ignored):
  a part not yet on plays `efon` (+0x8ac bit 2 set), one on and no longer near plays `efof`.
- The gate (flag 8, @0x26; FUN_10087890 returns it once DAT_104808a8 bit 1 is set, which a mode 0 does not clear):
  while it is non-zero FUN_100cd040 hides (+0xb2 | 0x20) any other entity of an ordinary class (+0x1d0 & 0xffffff1f,
  FUN_1008e290: PCs, NPCs, monsters, pets, party) whose gate (+0x13f & 0xf = +0x13c bits 24..27) differs from our
  non-zero one. The gates: 0x00D mask 4 u8 @0x44 low nibble (asm 0x1009aa6a), 0x00E mask 4 u8 @0x26 high nibble
  (0x1009c7f3), ours 0x037 u8 @0x5a high nibble (0x1009d8d1); LSB fills all three from the Confrontation / Elvorseal
  sub power. Ours: Entity.gate, World.my_gate, objective::gated in event.rs's hidden set. Live: Elvorseal sub power 13
  and a fence with gateId 13 hid the bot and the NPC beside Lnxcsfix; removing Elvorseal showed them again.
- Ours: client/border.rs (Parts, arc, update, remove; actor ids 0x0800_0000 | k; actor_place takes the arc). A
  removal stops the looping lp00 with the actor *(inf: retail frees the part's file with it)*.
- Live (Lnxcsfix in 230, both UIs): `!exec player:objectiveUtility({fence={pos={x=..,z=..},radius=..}})` red and blue
  walls (translucent blue panels, red / yellow bars) where the arc puts them: between the camera and the player for a
  line 2 yalms behind her, through her for a circle beside her; render 1 with the player 3 from the line: parts made,
  no efon, nothing drawn. Not compared with retail footage.

## c2s 0x017: asking again for a partly known entity (2026-10-28)

  u16 masks seen}) and call FUN_100fc830 = c2s 0x017 CHARREQ2 {ActIndex @4, UniqueNo2 @8 = the packet's id, UniqueNo3
  @0xc = the slot's id, Flg @0x10 = masks seen, Flg2 @0x12 = this mask} before storing: mask 0x20 frees the slot (id
  -1, masks 0), else masks |= mask and id = the packet's.
  - 0x00D (full 0x1f): same id: asks unless the masks seen or this mask already have all of 0x1f, or this is 0x20;
    another id in a used slot (not 0 / -1): asks unless this mask is exactly 0x1f.
  - 0x00E (full 0x17 for SubKind (@0x30 & 7) 1 / 7, else 7): another id in a used slot and this mask not exactly
    full: asks; then (any slot) the masks seen lacking a full bit and this mask lacking one and not 0x20: asks (so a
    brand-new NPC whose first update is partial asks at once, possibly twice).

## Grammar blocks from 0x80 and event op 0xc3 (2026-10-28)

- FUN_100bf790 sends a 0x01 block whose kind byte is 0x80 or more to FUN_100bdc50 (not the phrase builder). It
  appends the text as is (FUN_100c2d00); the args are FUN_100bdbe0 indices (0x40 | k a slot, 0x?2 a 14-bit packed
  index, computed in 16 bits):
  - 0x82: two words of file 55473 (0xd8b1, loader DAT_10663184) by num[a] and num[b] (as i16), joined by " " (the
    Pankration names, zone 71 "And in the blue corner is...").
  - 0x84: the name of op 0xc3 slot num[n] (n < 8; the slot itself unchecked), the racing chocobos' names in zone 70
    and the cities' chocobo lines.
  - 0x85: slot num[n]'s word, low byte (+0x6ec = 1, +0x6ed): FUN_100bdad0 then takes that alternative of the [a/b]
    group after the block ("...a [male/female]!").
  - 0x86: file 55474 (0xd8b2, expander +0x7f0) by num[n]: the chocobo name words ("Choose a word.").
  - 0x87 / 0x88 / 0x8a: language slots 0x1c (race names) by num[n], 0x22 (trust lines) and 0x1b (augments) by work[n]
    (expander +0x788 / +0x858 / +0x8c0, FUN_100bd820).
  - 0x89: group 12 0x1a2 + num[n] (0 past 0xb; a Unity leader) as "{%s} ", nothing for 0.
  - 0x81 / 0x83 (FUN_1022f330 / FUN_1022ec10 names) are in no dialogue file; not kept.
- Op 0xc3 (FUN_100bc000, len 7): slot val@1 (0..7) of DAT_10488210 (0x14 each) = the 16 bytes of str@3 and the word
  val@5. A slot outside 0..7 never advances in retail; ours waits there a frame at a time. The table outlives events
  (event_vm Memory.names).
- Ours: dialog::grammar_high, Texts::grammar (client/event.rs EventTexts: the two files, BattleText::grammar_line,

## Camera paths framed on actors (2026-10-28)

- A camera path's payload u32 @0 is an attach word (FUN_1003b900 copies it into the CMoCameraTask, whose actor and
  target are the scheduler's: FUN_1003a970 / FUN_1003a9f0). FUN_1003be10 (2019 FUN_1003afd0, the effect generators'
  attach switch) turns it into a frame on those actors.
- FUN_1003be40 (construction) takes the frame into task +0x20. Per frame (FUN_1003d220): with flags byte 1 (u32 @0x10
  bits 8..15) not 0 the frame moves toward a fresh one by byte / 255 (0x10329e94 = 1/255) per element.
- Count = keys + bit 19 + bit 20: 2 lerps in the world (the buffer +0xc4, no frame); 1 key (FUN_1003c970) is placed
  in a fresh frame; 3 or more: the spline's eye and target go through the task's frame (vtable +0x50).
- Zone 70's race cameras: rm00 / rm01 / rm04 attach 0x823 (mode 3: from the actor's point 2 toward the target's),
  byte 1 0xff; rm03 / rmat 0x821 (mode 1: the actor's point 2 in its matrix), rm03 byte 1 0x3c. The scheduler runs on
  npc040 with a chocobo as target (`sched_file #294, npc040, npc02e, 'rm01'`); keys are a few units around it.
  Ours drew them at their raw coordinates, near the world origin: a view of the sky under the map.
- Ours: CameraPath.attach (dat/title.rs), fx Effects::camera_frame (the shared attach switch, factored out of
  attach_matrix), event::camera_frame after the effects tick (the frame is one frame behind the actors *(ours)*), the
  blend scaled to retail's frame as 1/30 s *(inf)*; until the first frame a framed path keeps the last camera.

## MonStat idles: dft / df1, ark, hsr (2026-10-28)

Supersedes "Not done: the idle variants +0x1a8 / +0x1ac" under "Motion name bases".

- 0x00E (asm 0x1009be45..): with Flags1 bit 0 (byte @0x20, the monster flag) and Flags3 bit 26 (u32 @0x28) both
  clear, byte @0x2a bits 0..1 (LSB Flags3.MonStat) go to actor +0x124 bits 13..14; otherwise @0x2a is the
  sub-animation. FUN_10087dc0 reads them (or +0x12c bits 20..21 while +0x12c bit 19 is set: FUN_10087d80 /
  FUN_10087db0, an event-side override; not modelled).
- FUN_1008a1a0 with MonStat 2: idle +0x1a4 and +0x1a8 'dft ', the variant +0x1ac 'df1 ', walk +0x1b0 'ark ', run +0x1b4
  'hsr ', ignoring the bases. Otherwise all three idles take the base (+0x190, or +0x194 / +0x1a0 by state) and
  +0x1ac = +0x190 for statuses 2 / 7 on SubKind 0 models 0x3c0..0x3c9, 0x979..0x97d, 0x9bf..0x9c3.
- FUN_1008da00 per frame, for an NPC (UniqueNo high byte) not in statuses 3..5 (also +0x120 bits 7 / 13 clear and
  +0x170 = 0, and not those models in 2 / 7): +0x1ba -= the frame's ticks; below 0 it re-arms at 600 + rand % 600 and
  the idle becomes +0x1a8 or +0x1ac by rand & 1. Only MonStat 2 makes the two differ.
- Ours: net::EntityUpdate::mon_stat, Entity::mon_stat / idle_swap; a change marks the actor for a rebase, which takes
  the four names (and drops them again when MonStat leaves 2); actmotion::idle_swap. LSB never sets MonStat. A race
  model (Elvaan F) has no dft / df1 / ark (npc-shot: bind pose), so the motions belong to particular NPC models *(inf:
  not found yet)*.

## Training regime window (an Extra, 2026-10-28)

Not retail (retail has no tracker and no regime packet; the user's wish). client/regime.rs, Extras > Timers > Training
Regime (config `regime`, its drawer `regime_out`). The state comes from packets alone; nothing is sent for it:
- the book's event (an NPC named "Field Manual" / "Grounds Tome"): the start's num[7] is the server's regime id
  (0 or a hunt's 147..559: none); our update option 2 | page << 4 gets s2c 0x05C num[0..3] needed, num[7] the id; our
  end with that option (bit 31 repeat) and then s2c 0x02A with MesNum bit 15 about us is the accept, its installed id
  the block base R; option 3 (a Hunt Registry's 4) then 0x02A is a cancel; option 1 (Review) gets num[0..3] needed and
  num[4..7] killed;
- s2c 0x029 558 (about us: Data killed, Data2 needed) a credit, 559 complete, 643 begun anew; 6 / 20 (the defeated
  monster) name the credit's target when two slots need the same count (below).
- The names are never sent: the client's own zone dialogue holds them by id (R - 2050 + id a line per target,
  "[Siege Bat/Siege Bats]", "member[/s] of the worm family", "undead-type creature[/s]"; R + 3 + id the area), the
  same text the book shows. A book seen with a regime but no accept finds R as the entry "New training regime
  registered!" *(English only)*.
- The server re-sends nothing at login: the state is kept per character (regime/<name>.json beside the chat history).
  Credits with no page known make rows named after the monsters (or "Target n") until a book is visited.
- Window: classic on the Timers' dock under the Timers window (above it on the right), the area as its heading, a row
  per target "Siege Bat:" with "3/4" and a gauge (windowps 38 / 97), full rows dimmed; the drawer as the Timers'.
  Modern: an edge window ("regime", left edge at 0.6 by default) folding to a "Training" tab.
- Live (Lnxcsfix, Valkurm Dunes Field Manual, classic): page 1 accepted (regime 7: Hill Lizard 0/7, Sand Hare 0/1 shown
  at the "registered" line), credits 3/7 and 1/1 (`!exec player:messageBasic(558, k, n)`), the Review reset them to
  the server's 0/7 and 0/1, the cancel hid it; modern: a kills-only row "Target 1: 2/4", hidden by 559.

From the research notes:
- Id ranges in the book's bytecode (West Ronfaure's actor 0x010642dd, Gustav Tunnel's 0x010d4157): 1..146 FoV,
  147..559 hunts, 560..601 unused by LSB *(inf: elite training)*, 602..819 GoV. LSB: 146 FoV and 218 GoV pages in 60
  zones, up to 4 targets, the non-zero counts always a prefix.
- The book's start (s2c 0x034): num[1] page mask (bit p = page p hidden), num[2] cipher campaign, num[3] 1 with the
  key item Rhapsody in White, num[6] tabs, num[7] the current regime (a hunt's id while a hunt is on). Updates: 1
  review (needed num[0..3], killed num[4..7]; no 0x05C without a regime, so the VM sees num[0] = 0), 6 (FoV) / 5 (GoV)
  details (levels num[5] / [6]), 7 GoV prowess, 2 | page << 4 (FoV pages 1..5, GoV 1..10) a page. Ends: 2 | page << 4
  accepts (bit 31 repeat): 0x02A R | 0x8000, then (R + 1) | 0x8000; 3 cancels: (R + 2) | 0x8000; not enough tabs:
  (R + 1032) | 0x8000. An update or end is accepted only inside that book's event (a Talk within 6.0), so there is no
  Review without standing at a book.
- The book's event registers: Z0 the choice, Z1 the option, Z2..Z9 num[0..7]; menu rows by L6 (num[7]): 0 hides Review
  and Cancel, a FoV / GoV id hides "Read about individual training" (a new regime needs a cancel first), a hunt hides
  Review and Cancel.
- The zone dialogue's block (byte-identical in all 60 book zones, every regime id; R = the zone's "New training regime
  registered!", mapped through MsgShift): R - 2051 "The information on this page instructs you to defeat the
  following:", R - 2050 + id the targets (a line per non-zero slot k, `{0a 0k}`), R - 1026 + id the review list (`{0a
  0(k+4)}/{0a 0k}`), R - 2 "Target level range: ...", R - 1 the "Undertake this training regime?" prompt, R + 1 the
  job-change warning, R + 2 "Training regime canceled.", R + 3 + id "Training area: <zone>.", R + 1027 "(End of
  list.)". Line forms: 617 `{0a k} {7f 92 k}[Singular/Plural].`, 137 `{0a k} member{7f 92 k}[/s] of the <family>
  family.`, 5 `{0a k} <kind>-type creature{7f 92 k}[/s].`, separated by {07}. The event's constants hold the bases
  (zone 100: 8400 / 9424 / 10453).
- LSB's credit (checkRegime, for every alliance member in the zone): none when the member is dead, the id differs, in an
  alliance (unless the REWARD_ALLIANCE settings), the mob gives no EXP, or the slot is full (no message). A full page:
  559, for GoV a prowess line (609..620 / 625..636), once a Vana'diel day 565 (gil) and 566 (tabs), EXP, then with
  repeat 643 (counts back to 0) or the vars cleared: all in one tick. Before it the defeat (6 / 20) goes to everyone
  within 50 of the mob, so a member out of range gets 558 without it. A Hunt Registry (event 1500) end with option 4
  cancels: 0x02A REGIME_CANCELED "Current training regime canceled." *(inf for retail)*.
- LSB keeps the state in char vars only ([regime]type / zone / id / repeat / lastReward / needed1..4 / killed1..4),
  untouched by zoning, logout or a job change; retail cancels on a job change *(inf, from the R + 1 text)*.
- Attributing a 558 (k, n) (ours: it names no slot): the candidates are the slots with needed == n and killed == k -
  1 (with unknown counts, the unknown slots); one: it; several: the defeat within about 1 s whose name matches a
  specific label (singular or plural) or a family word as a word prefix ("Orc" ~ "Orcish"; not all: "Giant Guard" is
  Gigas, "Wespe" a bee, "Sand Digger" a worm, "Sagittarius X-XIII" an Antica); one family candidate left: it; else the
  lowest index (the next Review corrects swapped labels); none: the slot with needed == n nearest to k - 1. Of LSB's
  pages 94 have two slots with equal counts, 7 of them two families (FoV 74 Goblin / Orc; GoV 777, 778, 784, 790, 814,
  816).
- Retail: no tracker and no "regime" string in FFXiMain; the 0x029 queue (FUN_100c3480) special-cases only 1, 9, 0xb,
  0x32, 0x2cf, 0x2d, 0x32b, 0x32d, so 558 / 559 / 643 take the generic path into the log.

## Our upscale pack: four wrapped chunks, and the merge passes over broken images (2026-10-28)

- Crawlers' Nest (zone 197, file 297) drew its cave walls and floor untextured (the user's report): vana-upscale's
  ROM/0/76.DAT held "model dav_wf" as an 80-byte stub (header 2048 x 4096, no pixels). A 4x DXT3 of 512 x 1024 is 8 MB
  plus the header: its 19-bit size field (16-byte units) wrapped to 6 units. tex-pack halves such images since
  73b8575, but files built before that were kept by its resume. The merge took the stub over the stock / AshenbubsHD
  image, parse_img refused it, and every model on that texture lost it (92 of 170 models textured instead of 158).
- A scan of the whole pack (~/ffxi/lab/scratch/crawl/scan_pack.py: IMG payloads under 57 + w x h / 2) found 4: ROM/0/100.DAT,
  ROM/0/76.DAT and ROM5/0/27.DAT (dav_wf), ROM4/0/20.DAT (riz_wf01). Rebuilt with tex-pack (the four removed, halved
  now); the broken copies are in ~/ffxi/lab/scratch/crawl/broken_backup.
- dat/overlay.rs merge: a mod's D3s chunk too small for its own size (or with a bad size) is passed over, so the next
  mod's or the stock image stays (image_ok).

## Remote actors keep their level (2026-10-28)

User report: in multi-level zones (Crawlers' Nest) monsters and trusts are drawn a level above or below where they
fight, and cannot be seen or targeted.
- Correction: FUN_100c4390's 0.125-a-tick ease is the facing (+0x61c.., wrapped at +-3.1415 by _DAT_1031eba0 /
  _DAT_1031eb9c), not the position. The actor is drawn at the entity's slide: FUN_1008dfb0 and FUN_10091220 copy
  entity +4 to actor +0x34 every frame. Our 0.125 position ease is gone.
- FUN_1008b680: an actor with +0x120 bit 0x200 starts the frame's slide from its drawn position (+4 = actor +0x34),
  moves it (goal +0x24 - start) / remaining ticks a tick, or onto the goal when none remain; then if
  |goal - start|^2 > 144 (_DAT_103224e8) FUN_100911f0 copies the goal and its direction into the slide.
- FUN_1008dfb0: a grounded actor is snapped by FUN_1017a400 from the slide (+2 above it down 52, _DAT_1036b2bc = 50;
  else from 2 below up 15; FUN_10162590 takes every face, both sides, nearest to the start), and the result goes to both
  the slide y (+8) and the goal y (+0x28). The 0x00E handler does not snap the goal; only a new actor is snapped
  (FUN_10091220). So after one frame the goal stands on the actor's floor, and a goal sent on another level is more
  than 12 away and taken at once.
- Ours before: the goal was snapped at receipt from LSB's height, the drawn position eased and snapped on its own,
  and the slide's y was forced to the goal's every frame, so the 12-unit check never saw a height gap. An actor that
  once landed on the wrong level never came back: the eased y never got within 2 of the right floor. LSB's navmesh
  height can be more than 2 under the collision floor: Crawlers' Nest region c_196 at (57, -25): LSB -36.06, floor
  -38.08, the snap from LSB's height finds -10.61, 27 below.
- Now mod.rs slide_frame (test ground::remote_actor_keeps_its_level on zone 197): the slide from the drawn spot, the
  snap on the slide with the goal's height set from it, drawn at the slide. A goal at c_196's bad spot keeps a
  walking actor on its floor; an actor drawn below comes back when the next goal arrives.
- Knockback and op 0x7a pins: the slide goes on from the pushed / pinned spot, as retail's slide starts from the
  actor's position; with no slide time left the actor goes to the goal at once *(inf: LSB sends no position after a
  push)*.
- Probe: ground test snap_points (FLOOR_ZONE, FLOOR_POINTS: a TSV of id, name, x, y, z), fed LSB's region vertices
  (data/zones/<zone>/regions.yaml; spawns now live in data/zones/<zone>/mobs.yaml, mostly as regions, not in
  mob_spawn_points). Crawlers' Nest: 89 of 8392 vertices more than 1 off, most 1..2 at region edges against walls
  (a sloped wall face within 2 above), three on the wrong level.
- Live: Lnxcsfix in c_196 with Worker Crawlers about, no "floor:" diagnostic lines. The user's Nine run predates the
  diagnostic.

## Remote actors over holes in the floor (2026-10-28, not retail)

User report: in Garlaige Citadel, monsters and trusts fight from a level below around the holes in the floor.
- LSB's navmesh (navmeshes/<Zone>.nav, Detour with 32-bit refs, stored as x, -y, -z; reader
  ~/ffxi/lab/scratch/floors/navpts.py) crosses the rims of the pits. In Garlaige, 42 of its 10,787 points have no
  collision face within 3 of their height; 22 of them drop more than 8, most 12..20 (e.g. (-299.9, -0.2, 251): the
  floor under it is 19.75). Collision lists switched off in the file (0x2000): none in zone 200. LSB's own collision
  (ximeshes/<Zone>.ximesh: zlib, cells of block / placement pairs, a 3x3 column-major matrix and a translation; reader
  ~/ffxi/lab/scratch/floors/ximesh_at.py) has the same faces there as ours to the hundredth, so the holes are real
  and only LSB's navmesh crosses them.
- Retail's snap (part 1 above) drops an actor there, and one that stops over the rim to fight gets no goal that
  would bring it back. SE's servers never put an actor over a hole; LSB's do.
- Ours: slide_frame keeps the server's height along the slide, unsnapped (Entity.raw_y, the same linear slide as
  the position toward the sent height). A snap more than 8 under it stands the actor on the floor nearest that
  height within 3 (Ground::nearest), else holds it at that height. Test ground::remote_actor_stays_out_of_holes.
- Drops of 3..8 stay retail: in Crawlers' Nest 168 of 184 are navmesh points in the air over the floor just below,
  16 lie between two floors. Crawlers' Nest's navmesh has 27 points dropping more than 8, 5 of them 8..12 (which
  the 12-unit jump never brings back).
- The "floor:" diagnostic now compares with that height along the slide.

- Price counter (moneyctr), both UIs: Right on the ones place fills the top price of the item's price history (the
  history window's first row, the first of the last ten sales) for a sale and for a bid; retail clears to 0. A bid
  opened from the list's menu has no history window, so the history is asked in the background when its counter
  opens (search wire 5 / 6, the row's form); a history for another item is not used. Capped at the counter's max.
- The modern counter's buttons (-, +, x10, /10, All, 0 / OK, Cancel): Tab gives them the keys and back; Left /
  Right along a row, Up / Down between the rows, Enter presses the lit one. The digit's underline dims meanwhile.
- Search on the bid pages only (the category menus and the bid lists; not auc1, Sell or Sales Status): a field at
  the top ("Search the auction house"), reached by typing, a click, or Up off a menu's or list's top row (Down from
  the empty field gives the keys back). Hits from every bid category with their place as the note ("Weapons >
  Ammo&Misc. > Pet Items"); a pick opens the menus down to the category as Bid and its rows would, asks the list and
  puts the cursor on the item.
- The index: the search server's category lists (wire 0x15) hold every item of the category, in stock or not.
  Item records carry no AH category (LSB's item_basic.aH). All 60 categories are asked over one connection
  (net::search::ah_query_many; LSB's handler reads request after request on a socket), about a second for 10,721
  items, quietly 20 s after entering the world when no complete index exists, or at the first search ("Searching...").
  Kept in <data>/ah-index-<server>-<port>.tsv ("complete" or "partial", then item<TAB>category); category lists seen
  while browsing go in while it is partial; an item missing from the list its entry names drops the file.
- LSB's search server closes a sixth simultaneous session from one address ("More than 5 simultaneous connections",
  SearchHandler:69) and counts a finished session for some seconds after its reply (sequential queries 400 ms apart
  were still refused), with every client on the machine sharing the count. Ours now holds at most two search
  connections at once (net::search Slot), the friend list, Link List, level sync and search included.
- The list search's score (client/listsearch.rs) takes typos when nothing else matches: every query word within an
  edit (4..5 letters) or two (6+) of a name word or its start, a swap of neighbours one edit ("ghysal" finds Gysahl).

## Generator clones go with their last element (2026-10-28)

User report: casting Tonko: Ni left a looping effect on the caster. File 3154's `main` starts `gu01` and `gu00` with op
0x02 (duration 90 each). They are the same generator but for flag 0x1000 on `gu00` (0x1200 against 0x0200); both have
life 0, element life 90 (op 1 i16 @0x22) and an interval of 100 (rand(@0x64 = 0) + 1 + @0x66 = 99). Op 0x02 gives a
0x1000 clone no duration (asm 0x10058b93: FUN_1005d1e0 on the clone), so it is endless; ours re-emitted it every 100
ticks forever.
- Retail ends it another way. A generator's +0x18 low 15 bits are a reference count (FUN_10070ee0 up, FUN_10070f10
  down, walking +0x28 up to the file root). Each element holds its generator twice (FUN_10047150, and FUN_1004d920 asm
  0x100503c9). The element destructor FUN_10043b30 (current build FUN_10044970) drops them (asm 0x10043b90..0x10043b9a)
  and, when the generator is a clone (+0x1a bit 2, set by FUN_10052710's `|= 5`) and the count is 0, deletes it (asm
  0x10043bea..0x10043c15: FUN_10072b70, FUN_100731d0). So an unheld clone goes with its last live element, whatever its
  life or 0x1000: `gu00` shows one 90-tick element, as long as `gu01`.
- Held clones stay: the footstep dust and `i900` (the actor holds one), and an element's sub-clone while its parent
  element lives (+0x164, released at asm 0x10043b9f). Generators run as their own template never go this way: the
  unattached 0x1000 ones started at load, and op 0x02's unattached static path (asm 0x10058a41..0x10058a5f).
- Not the cause: the file's release (FUN_10073110 frees only files with a zero count, from the allocator under
  pressure; FUN_10047050 deletes a freed template's clones, which have no elements by then), the task's destructor
  (FUN_100564f0 never walks clones), the clone's +0x64 task link (read only by FUN_10041100 for damage numbers).
- Ours: fx Instance `clone` (op 0x02 off the template path, model-file generators) and `emptied`. An element that goes
  (expiry, a sound element's end) marks its clone. The end-of-frame sweep kills a marked clone still without elements
  after the generators' emissions *(inf: retail's order of generators and elements within a frame)*. Of the install's
  8216 actor-attached 0x1000 generators, 249 have element life + random below the interval and so end after one
  element, mostly in spell and ability files. Checked offscreen (`fx-shot 235 --file 3154`: nothing from 3154 is left
  once `main` ends; before, `gu00` stayed); the fx tests pass.

## A play start keeps the old motion's other regions (Shantotto II's orbs, 2026-10-28)

- FUN_100cb500: a new motion takes only the regions it has chunks for; the others go on with what they play. Ours
  moved the playing motion to `prev` when a scheduler or emote play started (actmotion::start / play_op), so the next
  pose saw no old motion and kept none of its regions. Over idle (Shantotto II's `idl` keys her orbs' bones 102..107
  in region 1) a region-0 spell motion then left region 1 to the status motion under the play only, and once the play
  ended into `run` (region 0 only) region 1 had nothing: the orbs stood still until she stood. Ours now takes the old
  motion from `prev` when the current one was just emptied. Live (Lnxcsfix /wave over `idl`): `wav keeps [None, None,
  Some("idl")]`, none before.
- The orbs' permanent freeze in the first report was the slot-keyed clones (see "Clones belong to their task by uid").
  Her orb generators are unaffected by "Generator clones go with their last element": element life 40 against an
  interval of 20.

## Ship actors: 0x00E SubKind 4, the XiModelActor (2026-10-29)

The boats and airships seen from the docks, the overhead airships, the pirate ship, the barge, the Manaclipper. Done
since "Ship voyages: the moving world" listed them as not done.
- 0x00E SubKind 4 (asm 0x1009cc43): kind 5, ship id u32 @0x34 (+0xf8; another id rebuilds the model), start u32 @0x38
  (+0x184, Vana'diel-epoch seconds); u16 @0x3c unused. The 0x00E position and heading reach the model actor only at
  its creation; server positions never move it afterwards (FUN_10092c20 skips kind 5). Ours: net.rs `ship`, Entity
  `ship` / `ship_rebuild`.
- The model (FUN_100c41f0 / FUN_100c4410): file id + 0x791c (ids 0..21 = 31004..31025), or the furniture table when
  the state is 0x37 at creation (props); MMB `fune`, else `_fun` (alpha tested), else the first; ids 0, 1, 2, 5, 6 keep
  their model generators off (entity +0x130 bit 1); the first 4 draws are skipped; on `fune` / `_fun` the heading
  eases 1/8 a tick toward its target (ours continuously, the same at 60 fps). Drawn as furniture (lit as the zone,
  'l_01' only, area 0), no shadow, no collision, no distance cull. Matrix T * Rx * Ry * Rz (FUN_100c4b50).
- States 0x12..0x19 play `seq0`..`seq7` (DAT_1032d42c) the frame they arrive (FUN_1008b460 returns 1 for kind 5):
  FUN_10097a80 / FUN_100c4730 kill the actor's running sequence (task +0x143, its drives with it) and start the new
  one; elapsed = now x 60 - start x 60 below 600 ticks plays from the first op, else the scheduler is caught up
  (FUN_100575a0: ops come due in turn, each told how long ago; generators still alive start part-way, sub-schedulers
  0x09 / 0x57 are caught up themselves, 0x1e / 0x26 / 0x27 / 0x3f run as normal, the rest is skipped). Bound to an
  event (op 0x4f), the start is now. Quiet under event op 0xab 5.
- Ops 0x26 / 0x27 (CMoPathDriveActorTask, fx/drive.rs): the Vtx spline over the op's duration, easing curves 0..4
  (FUN_10055ad0), flags @0x10 abs / face / forward, yaw0 @0x18; a new one kills the actor's drives; a child of its
  scheduler (it dies with it, before its step, so a backward drive never reaches its u = 1.0 end); the heading from
  the second frame (snap once, then the target when the step is >= 0.1; ours samples every 2 ticks). Ops 0xa9 / 0xaa
  (CMoActorRotationDriveTask): degrees, mode 0 holds, else linear. A drive made this frame places its actor without
  running its time *(inf: retail's first update is the frame after)*. A start's wait for its file is added to its skip
  (not the frame it was asked in).
- Ours: client/ships.rs (loads, the model actor, states, poses after each effects tick into the renderer's
  model_actors: own buffers and textures, drawn after the furniture), fx/drive.rs, fx/tasks.rs (start_sequence /
  kill_sequence, step_drives, fast_forward), FxActors (matrix, rotation, files, hidden, every point the position).
  Tests: the drive against the worked examples below (Selbina `seq0` from the staging point and caught up 1500
  ticks, Port Jeuno's descent with yaw / pitch, the pirate ship's leaving), the easing curves, the 22 ship files'
  MMBs.
- Live (Lnxcsfix, Port Jeuno): zoned in with the Bastok berth's `seq2` 7260 ticks old, caught up and drawn at the

  task unless world, clone +0xd0 = dur (+1 when 0), +0xd8 bits 14..27 = ftol(over). Ops 0x03 / 0x73 only resolve;
  0x09 / 0x57 / 0x85 fast-forward their sub-scheduler (FUN_10056b20 / FUN_10056ef0); 0x1e / 0x26 / 0x27 / 0x3f run
  with DAT_1047bf14 = over (only the path drive reads it).
- Op 0x26 / 0x27 (case asm 0x1005c954..0x1005cae8, ctor FUN_1005e890, update FUN_1005e9c0 / FUN_1005eef0; 10 words):
  +4 wait, +6 duration (x speed, FUN_1005e5b0), +8 the 4cc of a type-0x3e Vtx, +0xc its handle (FUN_10052870), +0x10
  flags (bit 0 abs, bits 1..2 face (bit 1 set: no pitch), bit 3 fwd, 4..7 unused), +0x14 curve 0..4, or > 6 the 4cc
  of a type-0x19 KeyFrame (cached at +0x20), clamped to 5, +0x18 f32 yaw0. 0x26 drives actor1 (FUN_10062770), 0x27
  actor2 (FUN_100627d0). It first kills every CMoPathDriveActorTask on that actor (FUN_1005e310 / FUN_1005e0e0) and
  needs the Vtx resolved (FUN_1004e3b0) and actor vt +0x178 *(inferred: "can be driven")*; the task (0xb0 bytes,
  vtable 0x1032b9a4) is a child of the scheduler task (FUN_10074790).
- Its update: left -= ticks; while left >= 0: u = left / total (1 -> 0), fwd: 1 - u; f = the curve, or the KeyFrame;
  apply; else, if it ever ran a frame, apply(path(1.0)) (literal 1.0, whatever fwd), then it ends. Apply: with face
  and started: d = p - prev, h = sqrt(dx^2 + dz^2), yaw = wrap(yaw0 - atan2(dz, dx)), pitch = atan2(dy, h) (with face
  bit 1 set an uninitialised local in retail; no file uses it; ours keeps the pitch *(inferred)*), no turn when h <
  0.1; abs: +0xd4 = p (FUN_100a57c0); relative: +0xd4 = position + (p - prev) once started; the first turn snaps
  +0x744 / +0xe4 / +0x44, later ones set the target +0xe4 only. Curves (FUN_10055ad0): 0 u, 1 sin(u pi/2), 2 1 -
  cos(u pi/2), 3 u <= 0.5 ? 0.5 sin(u pi) : 1 - 0.5 sin(u pi), 4 (1 - cos(u pi)) / 2, 5 without a KeyFrame u.
  Forward = (cos yaw, 0, -sin yaw); the bow is +x *(inferred)*. The spline in this build: FUN_10063c30 ->
  FUN_10063b80 (lazy build), FUN_100635b0, FUN_10063a60 / FUN_10063890.
- Op 0xa9 / 0xaa (ctor FUN_1005fa20, update FUN_1005fb30; 6 words): f32 @8 / @0xc / @0x10 the target in degrees (x
  pi/180, _DAT_1032a9f4), byte @0x14 mode, i16 @6 duration; the start = vt +0x1c0. Mode 0: every frame rot = target
  into +0x44, +0xe4 and +0x744, the time never running down (it holds until its scheduler ends); else left -= ticks, k
  = left >= 0 ? 1 - left / total : 1, rot = start + (target - start) k per component (no wrap) into +0xe4 / +0x44 (the
  model eases after it), ending below 0. The barge holds mode 0 before it side-steps into a berth (seq0 at t 1040: y
  -90; seq2 / seq4 -135; seq5 90; seq6 45).
- The frame FUN_100c47f0: +0x734 = +0xd4; `fune` / `_fun`: ceil(ticks) steps of +0x744 += (+0xe4 - +0x744) / 8 (y
  wrapped); else 'init' once, then +0x744 = +0xe4; +0x34 = +0x734 unless DAT_104568fc +9, +0x103 or +0x104. Draw and
  attach matrix: RotZ, RotY, RotX post-multiplied, then the translation (FUN_10027d10 / FUN_10027cf0).
- Lifetime: a task's destructor (FUN_100747c0 -> FUN_10074ad0) unlinks it and deletes its children (FUN_10074890).
  Every backward drive in the ship files is replaced by the next op 0x27 exactly at its end, or its scheduler ends
  then (Selbina `path` 0..1800 / `pat2` at 1800; Jeuno `pts0` 0..1600; `pts2` 900..2200), so at 30 fps the u = 1.0
  snap is never reached. So: a scheduler's ops step before its drives each tick, drives die with their scheduler in
  the same tick, and a starting drive kills the actor's running drives first.
- Worked examples (2-tick frames): Selbina `seq0` (2400 ticks; `path` 0..1800 abs, face, backward, curve 2, then
  `pat2` 1800..2400 abs, forward, curve 4): t 0 (-401.468, 0, -123.873) (the staging point), t 300 (-295.153, 0,

## The record loop's jump takes 0x32's wait back (bard songs on every target at once, 2026-10-29)

- User report: a song played its animation and sound on one target after another; retail plays them for everyone
  together. The user's log: a trust's song (file 3185) ran `hit1` on its targets about 3.8 s apart.
- File 3185's `main`: op 0x31, op 0x03 `hit1` (wait 15), op 0x32 (wait 215), end. Retail's op 0x32 (base FUN_10057000
  case 0x32): with a next record it moves actor2 to that record's target, then +0x98 (the countdown) -= this op's
  wait x speed (FUN_1005d5a0) and += the 0x31's (FUN_1005d5c0), and goes back to the 0x31. So only the last record
  waits 0x32's own wait: the targets come one loop body apart (15 ticks for the songs).
- Ours took 0x32's wait on every record. Now the jump takes it back (fx/tasks.rs op 0x32; test record_loop_waits).
  Not seen live. Melee rounds are split per record (combat::on_action), so their timing is unchanged.

## MZB names are XORed only in the encrypted versions (Jeuno interiors, 2026-10-29)

- User report: inside Lower Jeuno's Chamber of Commerce only the sky, the sea and some rails showed. The user's log:
  sub-area 464 loaded. Its file (564) has an MZB of version 0x1a, not encrypted, with plain placement names
  (`r3ju11_ligjt2`, the MMB's own spelling). We XORed every name with 0x55, so none of its 23 placements found a mesh,
  while the zone's stand-in for it was hidden.
- FUN_10179430: `bVar5 = mzb[3]`; the 0x55 XOR of each record's 16-byte name runs only when 0x1a < bVar5, the same
  bound as the decryption (decode_mzb, versions >= 0x1b). Ours now does the same (dat/zone.rs parse_mzb).
- Files with an MZB of version <= 0x1a in 30261006_0: zone 0 (0x17), sub-areas 326, 407, 464..466, 468..470,
  472..477 (0x1a). All of them drew nothing before. Checked offscreen (zone-shot 245 --sub 464) and live (Lnxcsfix
  inside the Chamber of Commerce, modern UI).
- The trigger point: FUN_10014390 passes our actor model's position (vtable +0x1bc, the +0x404 the doll moves; the
  second call is the same getter) to FUN_10181540 -> FUN_101760f0, so an event that moves our model moves it too.
  Ours took the network position. Event 20089 in Lower Jeuno (`!cs 20089`, Mumor) puts us at (-84.27, -6.0,
  -167.49), inside m6td (param 466, Mumor's room): before, the stand-in box showed; now 466 loads (seen live). Its
  own op 0x75 request is skipped with params 0, as LSB's `!cs` sends.
- That event ends on fdo1 with no fade-in (the server warps the player to Batallia Downs after it), so with `!cs`

- zone-info lists the sub-area triggers ('m' / 'M' records: class, param, box).

## Effect draw order: equal clamped keys draw in insertion order (Port Bastok's harbour, 2026-10-29)

- User report: the water in Port Bastok was far too dark. Arriving by airship at Vana'diel 12:07 it measured (10,
  11, 12), black. On a fresh login it was navy (about (31, 45, 54) at noon), and after another landing a light
  lavender (the night fog colour).
- The harbour is three zone generators on one spot (t_ba/effe/esea): `down` (mesh col1, colour 0x96000000, blend
  0x44, op 0x30 bias 5000), `col1` (mesh col1 untextured, 0x96808080 with R / G / B keyed by rtms / gtms / btms,
  0.099 / 0.157 / 0.2 at noon, blend 0x44, bias 4500) and `1sea` (mesh 1sea, texture sea01, 0x78787878 keyed by
  semt, additive, bias 4000, UV scroll). All three have template flags 0x401000: bit 22 makes the key the bias
  alone, bit 12 writes depth. By y they lie down 9.9, col1 9.87, 1sea 9.84 (y down).
- Retail's ordering table (FUN_10054410, asm 0x100544a5): the key is clamped to [0, 512] for the bucket, and the
  walk compares that clamped key with each node's raw key, so a key at the clamp goes after every node in the
  bucket. All three keys clamp to 512 and draw in insertion order. Elements insert in their own update
  (FUN_10044c00 / FUN_10044ca0 -> FUN_10044ab0 -> FUN_10054600), i.e. in task-list order. The default list
  (FUN_10074170) appends a task, or puts one made during another task's update just before that task. So a
  generator's new elements run just before it, in creation order, and generators run in start order.
- Ours tied the three at 512 and fell back to element slot order. With depth writes, the order decides the look:
  col1 / 1sea first hide `down` (navy with the sea texture); 1sea first hides col1 (the fog colour through the
  additive sea); `down` after col1 at a grazing event camera came out black. Now ties go by the generator's start
  serial, then the element's (fx/mod.rs `insert_order`), so the harbour draws col1, 1sea, down every time. Seen
  live after a login and after an airship landing (both navy); offscreen unchanged.
- The navy itself is the data: untextured MMB `rgb = sat(2·D·F)` ("Effect generators") with D = 0x73 and F =
  (0x19, 0x28, 0x32) gives about (23, 36, 46), then fog. Not compared with a retail screenshot.
- mmb-dump prints each model's blending word and vertex colour mean / range.

## Skillchain helper and the battle menu's suggestions (ours, 2026-10-29)

- Not retail (the skillchain add-ons; user's spec 2026-10-29: "a flyout ... anytime we're in a party, what skillchains
  we can make and what their elements are"). The client has no table of skill properties: the server applies them.
  So the data is LandSandBoat's, bundled as `crates/vana-client/data/skillchains.txt`. It is made by
  `vana-client skillchain-gen --lsb ~/landsandboat` from sql/ weapon_skills, mob_skills, pet_skills, blue_spell_list
  and mob_skill_lists (209 weapon skills, 359 mob / pet skills with properties, 52 blue spells, 52 trust lists).
  dat/skillchains.rs holds the rules, taken from battleutils.cpp:
  - `skillchain_map`: a closer's property against the resonance's, in the resonance's order (FormSkillchain);
  - the chain's elements (GetSkillchainMagicElement);
  - the levels: 1 for Transfixion .. Impaction, 2 for Gravitation .. Fragmentation, 3 for Light / Darkness, 4 for
    their second level.
- Timing as LSB applies it (GetSkillChainEffect):
  - an opener leaves its properties on the monster for 10 s;
  - a closer counts only when it lands more than 3 s after the last skill;
  - each chain link takes 1 s off the window;
  - the magic burst window is open while a chain (tier above 0) stands.
- The chain made comes from the 0x028 record's proc. ActionProcSkillChain's kind maps to a property: 1 Light,
  2 Darkness, 3 Gravitation, 4 Fragmentation, 5 Distortion, 6 Fusion, 7 Compression, 8 Liquefaction, 9 Induration,
  10 Reverberation, 11 Transfixion, 12 Scission, 13 Detonation, 14 Impaction, 15 / 16 the second Light / Darkness.
- client/skillchain.rs follows each monster the party hits:
  - a weapon skill (category 3), mob skill (11, 13; trusts and pets) or blue spell with properties opens a resonance
    on every target it hit;
  - a proc makes the chain instead;
  - a monster's last party target is kept from its melee, spells and skills (for the suggestions).
- Each member's skills:
  - ours from the weapon skill list;
  - a trust's from its LSB skill list, by name; one skill under several ids is shown once;
  - anyone's as seen used.
  `combos` lists every chain two members can make, strongest first; `closers` lists what closes the open resonance.
- Modern (modern/extras.rs): an edge window, right edge under the minimap by default, shown in a party of two or more.
  - On the target (or the latest resonating monster): the properties, or "Skillchain: X" in gold with "Burst
    <elements> on <monster>: N s"; who used what; a bar for the 3 s wait, then for the window left; up to 6 closers
    with the chain and element icons.
  - "Party chains": each chain once with its elements and up to two ways (ours first; an opener with 1000 TP
    bright), "and N more".
  - It ends above the next panel under it on its edge (the target and party windows), and long lines end in an
    ellipsis.
- Classic (skillchain.rs's window): a game-art window docked with the Timers, under the Timers and training regime
  windows (above them on the right), 240 wide. Its drawer folds it like theirs. The same content in text lines,
  elements by name; `topbar-shot --window skillchain:DOCK` draws a sample.
- Seen live (Lnxcsfix with a Bronze Sword, Naji and Ayame, an immortal Tunnel Worm in South Gustaberg):
  - Ayame's Tachi: Yukikaze opened Induration / Detonation, and the window showed the wait;
  - Fast Blade 1 s after it opened a new Scission, as LSB rules it (too early to close);
  - Fast Blade then Burning Blade 4.5 s later made "Skillchain: Liquefaction", "Burst Fire", and listed Vorpal Blade
    / Goten to continue it into Fusion.
- Suggestions (suggest.rs, rewritten): rules over facts taken every half second, at most four, each with its reason.
  - In order: raise, shadows (Utsusemi with no Copy Image), ailments, healing (Curaga for three, else the Cure tier,
    a waltz with no cure), burst the chain made with the strongest nuke of its elements, close the open resonance
    with the strongest closing weapon skill (with the wait left), Provoke / Flash when the monster hits a non-tank,
    job abilities for the fight (Berserk ... Third Eye when targeted, Sneak Attack before a weapon skill), Yonin
    while targeted else Innin, a samba, debuffs missing on the monster (Dia / Bio, Slow, Paralyze, Blind, Gravity, the
    ninjutsu, Elegy, Requiem), open a chain a partner with TP can close, the strongest weapon skill, renew our
    buffs under 30 s, and Protect / Shell / Reraise between fights.
  - They head the root battle menu (modern), not each list. Up from the first command walks into them, Enter or a
    click takes one: the ability or spell list opens on it and Enter, so retail's target prompt follows. A
    suggestion that names a member starts that prompt on them.
  - Seen live: "Provoke: the Tunnel Worm is attacking Naji", "Fast Blade: closes the open chain in 2.7 s: Scission
    (Earth)", "Red Lotus Blade: opens Fusion (Light, Fire) with Naji's ...". Up, Up, Enter, Enter used Provoke; a
    click on Berserk opened its prompt.
- Not seen live: bursts (no caster in the test), the classic window in a live party (offscreen only), blue magic as a
  skill.
- (2026-11-03) Casters: the debuffs come whenever a monster is the target, engaged or not, two at most at once (Poison
  / Poison II added). A nuke rule: the elemental spell of the element the target resists least, by LSB's
  rank_element (data/resistances.txt from `python3 -I data/resist_gen.py ~/landsandboat OUT`: data/ecosystems.yaml's
  ecosystem, family and species layers merged as dataset.cpp merges them, and zones/*/mobs.yaml's templates by zone
  and shown name: 499 species, 13,070 monsters; dat/resists.rs), then the element today's weather (LSB weather ids
  4..19 in pairs) or day strengthens, then single-target, then MP. A spell suggestion stands for its family when the
  family has more than the one spell castable now: an elemental nuke's element (tiers, -ga, ancient magic), else the
  name without its tier and area form (Protect / Protectra, Cure / Curaga, Dia / Diaga ...). Its row reads the family's
  name with the more mark; Right, Enter or a click opens the spells beside the battle menu (single-target first,

## Actor culling: every +0xb2 reason hides the model and the plate (2026-10-29)

- Retail (below; MODLOG "Tab candidates"): an actor with +0xb2 bit 0 set is not drawn at all.
  The update queues no draw entry, the list walk FUN_10082d70 skips vt+0x288, and the queued callback re-checks.
  The reasons: no skeleton box, wholly behind the near plane, past the draw distance, not faded in, off the viewport,
  or failing FUN_1006c280's occlusion test.
- The name plate goes too: FUN_100819d0 (the plate's draw test) returns 1 only when u16 +0xb2 == 0 (and the names
  flag); our own plate likewise, and none in first person (vt+0x304 with DAT_10475578).
- Ours before: only the draw distance (far_out) hid the model; the rest only kept Tab off (World::visible).
- Now:
  - the actor draw list and the refraction list drop a skinned character not in `visible`;
  - its plate goes the same way (doors by their 0.6 cube test);
  - ours is never culled by these tests;
  - actors without a skeleton (props, ships, furniture) are drawn as before.
  - The occlusion test keeps running on culled actors (their queries come from tests 1-5), so they come back when
    the scene depth behind them clears; a result is a frame or two late (retail tests every 4th frame).
- Seen live in Port Bastok: NPCs in view drawn with their names through a camera turn (Gwinar at a distance), no pop.

From the research notes:
- The draw distance test in the actor update FUN_100c63d0 (asm 0x100c7d12..0x100c7d66): when u16 +0xb2 == 0 and an env
  is loaded, D_a = FUN_1018b8f0(E, 1) (the scenery's value at any setting) against the farthest skeleton box corner's
  view depth (-min z_view, stored to +0x8c); deeper -> +0xb0 = 1, +0xb2 |= 1. Exempt (bit cleared, +0x8c = +0xbc =
  0.1): our actor (vt+0x304) while DAT_10487f80 is set *(inferred: first person)*, or a stack flag not identified.
- The draw entry is queued only when u16 +0xb2 == 0 (+0x8d0 = 0x100cbd90, +0x8d4 = self, key +0x8c8 = depth x 512 +
  +0x8ec, inserted into DAT_1047bc94 by FUN_100553c0); else +0x8d4 = 0. FUN_10082d70 calls vt+0x288 (FUN_100cbd60 ->
  FUN_100cbde0) only for u16 +0xb2 == 0 and +0x8c >= 0 (else it sets +0xb0 / +0xb2 bit 0); the queued callback
  re-checks both; FUN_100cbde0 marks the actor culled and returns when FUN_1002b5a0 yields nothing *(inferred: no
  skeleton)*.

## Lamp Lights: real point lights in place of baked lamplight; soft glows (ours, 2026-10-29)

- Not retail (the parked plans B and C of "Effect fixes from the San d'Oria gate lamps"; the user asked for them
  2026-10-29). Settings > Effects > Lamp Lights: Baked (retail) / Real, default Real (config `lamp_lights`).
- Lamps (client/lamps.rs, Effects::lamp_scan, every second):
  - lamps are the zone's live glow meshes whose group textures start "light" ('ltla', "light   lanp");
  - glows within 1.5 yalms merge into one lamp;
  - a lamp within 4 yalms of a kind-0x47 data light is lit already (San d'Oria's gl01..gl04 by glr / gll);
  - each other lamp takes the nearest data light as its template;
  - its light stands 0.7 yalm out from the nearest wall within 2 yalms (Ground::raycast in 8 level directions), else
    at the glow.
  - Positions come from the elements' readback (back.world); slots are the free ones after the zone's light keys, up
    to 254 (an actor's 8-bit light index).
- The shells: untextured MMB meshes in a glow generator's folder (gin1 'san_') are hidden (element `hidden`: updated,
  not drawn).
- The light table (render/effects.rs lamp pass, after the effects update): each lamp slot takes its template's range,
  colour and intensity at the lamp's position, so dusk, dawn and switching off follow the data.
- Scenery: ZoneRenderer::set_lamps puts lamp slots into the free light slots of every zone instance whose bounding
  sphere is within 16 of the lamp, nearest first. Only the light words are written, after a streamed zone is up, and
  a stand-in coming back keeps them. Actors: lamps::offer fills the floor's free light slots within 16 yalms
  (actor_lamp picks the strongest, as for data lights).
- Soft glows: the effects draw copies the scene depth (depth targets now have COPY_SRC) before its passes, when a
  flag-27 element (glows and light volumes, sort key + 400) draws. It is bound at group 0 binding 7. Such an element's
  alpha is multiplied by sat(scene depth - its depth) in yalms; the scene depth is linearised with the draw's near
  and far.
  - Tried on the glow sprites too (lk01.., glk1.., texture 'light'): their core sits against the lantern model and
    faded to nothing, so only flag 27.
  - The halo blotches on the tunnel walls are in the wall textures themselves (they show in every variant).
- zone-shot runs the lamps after its effect ticks (one extra update so the slots are filled before the next frame):
  FFXI_NO_LAMPS shows the baked look, FFXI_LAMPS_DARK the shells hidden without lamp lights.
- Seen: zone 101's gate tunnel (offscreen at 2:00 and 19:30) lost the shell's light triangles on walls and ceiling
  beams, and gl05..gl11 light the pillars and floor in pools. Live in East Ronfaure: 11 glows, 13 data lights, 1
  shell, 7 lamp lights on 17 instances.
- Not done: sub-area (interior) instances get no lamp slots; lamps without any data light in their zone get no light.

## Actor ground shadows (FUN_10032f80; 2026-10-29)

- The mode gate FUN_100c9da0, light and size FUN_10033080 (2019 build; more at the end), the three
  draws FUN_1017dd50 / FUN_1017e0b0 / FUN_1017ecf0). Config 0x3a: High 2, Normal 0, Off 1.
- Modes (client/shadows.rs `mode`):
  - 1, the silhouette: ours (our mount's instead while riding; our own rod too), and everyone in High;
  - 0, the projected blob (2 past view depth 20): every other PC, NPC and monster;
  - 2, the quad: those standing on a covered face;
  - none: others' riders, rods and Indi auras; feet more than 2 above the eye; zone 33 on surface kinds 8 / 9.
- The entity flags (FUN_1008dfb0, latched on the actor when its model is made):
  - +0x12c bit 10 (0x00D / 0x00E u8 @0x27 bit 1; LSB NPC name_prefix bit 1) or bit 11 (event op 0xa5): no shadow;
  - bit 12 (event op 0xc0): no blob, the silhouette still draws.
- Not ported: the "nothing drawn on the first frame" rule (+0x728 < 2, inferred) and chairs (they have no actor here).
- GPU (render/shadow.rs), per frame:
  - compute `prep`: the dominant light (the strongest point light in range of the floor's four, else the sun's travel
    direction negated), below the horizon (0.45, -0.9, 0), eased 0.04 a tick in a per-caster state slot, held at 40.9
    degrees under 60, S from the box corners seen from the light (5 / 9 for blobs), and the silhouette view-projection;
  - silhouettes: each mode-1 actor skinned flat white into its own R8 layer (PerspectiveFovRH pi/16, aspect 1, eye
    pos - 12 S L), the layers at the scene's size as retail's one target, as many as fit in 128 MB (at most 32;
    the nearest get them, the rest blob);
  - one pass over the scene: quads, then per collision cell instanced blob and silhouette draws on the cached faces
    (`Ground::cell_tris`: the decal faces for blobs; for silhouettes geometry word 0 without the normal test, door
    boxes left out), blend ZERO / INVSRCCOLOR, MODULATE2X, depth tested, no depth write, z bias 15, no fog.
- The cell faces are cached per (x, z, kind) and dropped when a sub-area's ground goes in or out.
- Seen live in East Ronfaure: Normal draws our silhouette at our feet (at 512 its edges were stair-stepped, so the
  layers went to the scene size) and small blobs under Croteillard and Rayochindot (S/3 across, as read). High gives
  Croteillard a silhouette lying the same way as ours; Off draws none.
- Not seen: point-light shadows indoors, the quad under cover, riding, ops 0xa5 / 0xc0.

From the research notes:
- Call chain (2019 addresses, current ones in the last bullet): the actor draw -> FUN_100c9da0 (mode, light, size) ->
  the mesh draw FUN_1002a8c0 -> FUN_10032f80 (ECX actor+0x6bc, the shadow object) right after the actor's meshes.
  Nothing for +0xb2 != 0, +0x8c < 0, or a draw alpha min(1, (+0x664 < 0.8 ? +0x664 x 1.25 : 1) x +0x59c) under 0.0001
  (first person fades the player out: no shadow).
- FUN_10032f80: mode >= 3 nothing; 2 the quad unless noblob (u16 actor+0x670); 1 the ground pass when the silhouette was
  drawn this frame (shadow +4, then cleared); 0 unless noblob, the projected blob at view depth < 20, else the quad.
  size_b = S / 3, size_s = 2.4 S.
- The gate in FUN_100c9da0, first match wins: zone 33 on floor surface 8 / 9; actor+0x66c == 0; Off; feet over 2 above
  the eye -> none. High and depth < 40 -> 1, where depth is the global the previous actor left (0 after any mode 1), so
  in High every actor that gets this far gets 1 at any distance (retail's outcome). Then depth = actor+0xbc. Ours:
  riding a chocobo / mount -> none, else 1. Others: +0x728 (primitives of its last mesh draw) < 2 -> none *(inf: its
  first drawn frame; not ported)*; a main actor riding -> none; an extra actor by kind +0xa4: chocobo 1..4 / mount 0x54
  -> 1 when we ride it, else B; rod 5..0x24 / chair 0x3d..0x51 -> 1 when ours, else none; Indi aura 0x25..0x3c, 0x52,
  0x53 -> none; others B. B = the covered flag actor+0x17c ? 2 : 0.
- +0x66c is 0x80 when the model colour's alpha (+0x663) is non-zero, else 0 (ctor default 0x80) *(inf, not traced:
  whether a 'spop' actor's alpha-0 start colour is already set then)*.
- Light: vt+0x404 non-zero -> straight up (0 in every skeleton vtable). Else FUN_100c94a0's pick from the actor's five
  D3DLIGHT8 slots (+0x388 + 0x68 i): the point light in range with the largest 1 / max(d² x Attenuation2, 1e-4), else
  the first directional, else slot 0. Point: L0 = Position - pos; directional: -Direction. FUN_10033080 ends with |L.x|
  and |L.z| < 0.01 -> L.x = 0.01.
- Quad FUN_1017dd50: a strip (±1, -0.001, ±1), diffuse 0x80606060, WORLD = scale(size_b, 1, size_b) x translate(pos):
  flat at the actor's y, never following slopes; POINT, CLAMP.
- Projected blob FUN_1017e0b0: per collision face its object matrix, CULL CCW (CW when mirrored, +0xa4 bit 0); uv =
  (W.xz - pos.xz) / size_b + 0.5, a diameter of S / 3, half the quad's (the switch at depth 20 doubles the blob, as
  read); diffuse c = 0x60 - trunc(48 |W.y - pos.y|) clamped >= 0, ARGB (0x80, c, c, c); a face with all three c negative
  is dropped (a 2-unit fade).
- Silhouette FUN_100329e0 / FUN_10032c50: one A8R8G8B8 target at the scene's size, shared; each mesh draw of a mode-1
  actor (depth < 4) is repeated into it, the first one clearing it to 0. TEXTUREFACTOR 0x80FFFFFF, stage 0 SELECTARG2
  TFACTOR (cutouts fill solid), lighting, fog and z off; alpha test GREATER 0x60 passes; blending off *(inf)*. Its frame
  is 2 x 12 S x tan(pi/32) = 2.364 S wide at the actor; the ground pass uses 2.4 S.
- Ground pass FUN_1017ecf0: hl = |L.xz|, u = dot(W - pos, (L.z, 0, -L.x) / hl) / size_s + 0.5, v = dot(W - pos, (L.x, 0,
  L.z) / hl) / size_s + 0.5 (the head away from the light, not mirrored); c = 0x40 - trunc(32 |dy|); LINEAR, CLAMP.
- kage_tex (file 0x1b8c): maru / kage (DXT3 256 x 256, no mips) / end, a grey cone from 255 at the centre to 0 at radius
  ~124 of 128, alpha 0x88 unused. Peak darkening: blob 0.75, silhouette 0.50.
- ZBIAS is 2 on an ATI adapter (vendor 0x1002), else 15. *(Not traced: whether the overlay passes between the meshes and
  the shadow leave other stage states.)* Overlapping shadows multiply; the actor's alpha is ignored until under 0.0001;
  later actors and translucent effects (harbour water) draw over a shadow.
- 30261006_0: FUN_100c9da0 = FUN_100cbde0, FUN_1002a8c0 = FUN_1002b6e0, FUN_10032f80 = FUN_10033da0, FUN_10033080 =
  FUN_10033ea0, FUN_100328f0 = FUN_10033710, FUN_100329e0 / FUN_10032c50 = FUN_10033800 / FUN_10033a70, FUN_1017dd50 =
  FUN_10184c90, FUN_1017e0b0 = FUN_10184fe0, FUN_1017ecf0 = FUN_10185ca0, FUN_101720a0 (the kage_tex lookup) =
  FUN_10178f90; mode / depth / S / noblob DAT_1045b77a / b80c / b810 / b814, config 0x3a DAT_10456acc, the scene
  DAT_10631f24.

## Our upscale pack: dithered glows and DXT3 banding (2026-10-29)

- Seen live at dusk in East Ronfaure: a translucent checkerboard over the San d'Oria gate. Not the renderer (it went
  with vana-upscale off, stayed with Lamp Lights off): zone 101's `light   light` / `light   lanp` glows have
  dithered alpha at 64 x 64, which bilinear filtering hides at 1x; Upscayl kept each dither dot as a hard 4 x 4 square
  (and drew an "X" across `lanp`).
- Undithered: textures whose visible pixels are mostly partial alpha (at least half) and whose alpha gradients are
  pixel dither (the share of gradient pixels that are a peak or pit across a row or column, >= 0.25): 2,270 images,
  blurred premultiplied (Gaussian sigma 0.7, float) before Upscayl. Scripts in ~/ffxi/lab/scratch/checker
  (dither_scan.py, undither_lib.py, undither_all.py, apply_undither.py); the earlier upscales in
  ~/ffxi/lab/scratch/upscale/up_dithered.
- That showed DXT3's 4-bit alpha: halved to the PS2 scale a smooth glow has about 8 levels and banded. tex-pack now
  error-diffuses (Floyd-Steinberg) the alpha onto the 16 levels for translucent images (half the visible pixels
  partial). Rebuilt: every translucent image's encoding, 8,898 DATs.
- Offscreen (zone-shot 101 at 20:15 from (80, -64.5, 268)): the halo is smooth, close to stock.

## Config tool 0019 "2-D Mapping" (2026-10-29)

- Retail (FUN_10038c40, cur FUN_10039a80; more at the end of this entry): category 10
  (flag-0xB1 images with the u32 at payload 57 low nibble 10: the 209 palettized `menumap` images) are made DXT3 when
  0019 is 0 (Compressed), uncompressed when 1 (Full). The DXT map images are used as stored either way.
- Ours: client/map.rs `decode` (the map window, the overlay, the minimap): with 0019 = 0 (render::MAP_COMPRESSED,
  set at start and by Settings) a category-10 image goes through texpresso BC2 and back (ClusterFit), the lossy
  surface retail's D3DX load gives *(inf: D3DX's encoder differs in detail; the blocks are the same kind)*. Takes
  effect at the next map load (Settings row NextZone). Test map_category_10_through_dxt3.

From the research notes:
- 0019 = DAT_10456ab0 (2019 DAT_10444198), FFXiMain default 1 (Full). 2019 addresses unless marked cur.
- FUN_10038c40: the category is (+0x2c >> 4) & 0xf, which FUN_1001cb10 (the IMG parser) sets only for flag-0xB1
  images, from the low nibble of the u32 at payload offset 57 (the palette follows at 61). For images not already DXT:
  category 9 always uncompressed; 10 uncompressed when 0019 != 0; any other uncompressed when 1 <= category <= 0018,
  else compressed. Uncompressed: A8R8G8B8 (0x15) for 24 / 32-bit sources, A1R5G5B5 (0x19) for 16-bit. Compressed: DXT1
  for 16-bit sources, DXT3 for 24 / 32-bit (the palette entry size, IMG byte 53, is 0x20 for maps); FUN_10039010
  converts to A8R8G8B8 and D3DX loads that into the DXT surface. Flag-0xA1 files ("1TXD" / "3TXD") are used as stored.
- Install scan: exactly 209 images are 0xB1 category 10, all `menumap m_###_##` (512 x 512, 8-bit, a 1024-byte BGRA
  palette); the other 676 map images are 0xA1 DXT3. Category 9 = 539 images (`cntguide...`), untouched by 0019.

## Config tool 0040 "Graphics Stabilization" (2026-10-29)

- Retail (FUN_10024e10, cur FUN_10025c40; more at the end of this entry): the actor shine
  pass sets D3DRS_WRAP0 = 7 when 0040 is 0 (Off, the default; also not on the listed Intel fallback device), so each
  generated coordinate runs the short way round the 0 / 1 seam across a triangle; On interpolates plainly.
- Ours had only the plain form (= On). Now vs_skinned_shine reads its triangle's first corner from the skinned vertex
  buffer (bound as storage at group 3 binding 1; the draws are non-indexed lists, so a triangle is vertex_index / 3),
  skins its normal the same way and takes each coordinate relative to it (s0 + d - round(d)) when the shine uniform's
  uv.z is 1 (render::SHINE_WRAP, 0040 == 0). Each skinned model makes its shine group once (Skinned::shine). Settings'
  row is live.
- FFXI_SHINE_TEST puts a striped shine on our own actor (checks; no effect file needed). Seen live with it, wrap on and
  off: the pass draws, no errors; the difference is limited to triangles whose corners' normals differ widely in x / y.
- fx-shot honours 0040 (it draws no actor models, so it cannot show the shine).

From the research notes:
- 0040 = DAT_10456a74 (2019 DAT_1044415c), default 0. 2019 addresses unless marked cur.
- WRAP0 = 7 (wrap U, V and W of coordinate set 0) needs 0040 == 0 and DAT_103c75f8 +0x5c == 0 (+0x5c: the device was
  made on the fallback path for listed Intel chips, FUN_10014a50 / FUN_10002ce0); FUN_10025140 sets WRAP0 = 0 after
  the pass. The generated coordinates: s = 0.5 n.x + 0.5 + U, t = 0.5 n.y + 0.5 + V. Whether drivers applied WRAP0 to
  generated coordinates varied *(inf: the reason for the setting)*.
