## Config tool 0011 "Environment Animation" (2026-10-29)

- Retail: MMB loader FUN_10168eb0, per-draw FUN_101734f0, curve FUN_10053550, curve tables FUN_10160700 /
  FUN_10160830 / FUN_101606a0; more at the end of this entry.
- Data: dat/zone.rs keeps the type-2 vertices' delta (@12 of the 48-byte vertex; Vertex::delta, Mmb::animated) and the
  curves (sway_curves: per SWAY_TAGS weather tag the type-0x19 chunks of `weat/<tag>/kfrm`, else `mode/kfrm`, at
  most 32; (t, value) pairs up to t = 1). Zone 101 has mode/kfrm only (one curve for every tag); Jugner (104) has
  weat/fine/kfrm and no mode/kfrm, so its animated meshes stand still in any other weather (retail too, as read).
- GPU (render/sway.rs): per animated instance a (timer, curve) state, the timer from rand() % 300, the curve picked
  on the first frame. A compute pass per frame, before the culling copies the instances: the timer advances by the
  frame's ticks; past 300 it wraps and picks a curve of the current weather; s = max(0, 1 - curve(timer / 300)),
  k = floor((N - 1) s) / (N - 1) with N = 1 / 16 / 32 for Off / Normal / Smooth, written into the instance's area.y.
  vs_main adds k x delta (vertex flags >> 8 index the deltas at globals binding 4; retail draws position buffer
  trunc((N - 1) s) of N baked ones, the same quantised offsets). Mesh boxes include pos + delta for the culling.
- Not modelled: undrawn instances keep advancing (retail advances an instance only when drawn *(inf: call site)*);
  the random picks are a hash, not rand(). Sub-areas share the zone's globals and get no deltas (none seen animated).
- Seen: zone-shot of La Theine (102) by an animated instance: the dandelions' heads move between Off and Smooth;
  live in East Ronfaure (2412 animated instances, 6118 deltas) with no errors.

From the research notes:
- 0011 = DAT_10456ac0 (2019 DAT_104441a8), FFXiMain default 1 (Normal; ours 2). 2019 addresses unless marked cur.
- The type-2 vertex (48 bytes): pos f32x3 @0, delta @12, normal @24, BGRA colour @36, uv @40; triangle lists. The
  loader keeps N (+0x64: 1 / 16 / 32), the animated flag +0x68 (0011 != 0) and +0x6c = float(N - 1), one static buffer
  per piece (stride 0x18: normal, colour, uv; stream 1) and N position buffers (stride 12, stream 0) holding pos + (i
  / (N - 1)) delta. Normals do not move.
- Both scenery draw paths (FUN_10175ac0 after its distance tests, FUN_10176f20) call FUN_101734f0 (cur FUN_1017a3f0)
  when +0x68 is set, then bind buffer trunc((N - 1) x inst+0x15c) (asm 0x10176df9). The instance record: +0x154 the
  first call, +0x158 timer, +0x15c s, +0x160 the curve; the timer runs on FUN_10014000 (1/60 s ticks). The curve
  (FUN_10053550): piecewise linear over (t, value) pairs, t clamped to [0, 1], walked until t >= 1.0.
- Curves: FUN_10160700 (zone set-up) fills zone +0x34428 for 20 weather tags (fine suny clod mist dryw heat rain sqal
  dust sand wind stom snow bliz thdr bolt aura ligt fogd dark); FUN_10160830 collects up to 32 per tag (the
  `mode/kfrm` fallback through FUN_100712e0 from the weather node *(inf)*); FUN_101606a0 picks one at random for the
  current weather (FUN_10181090 of DAT_106175ac). La Theine (DAT 202): `mode/kfrm/k001` values 0..0.44,
  `weat/wind/kfrm/k001` up to 0.90.
- Scan of the zone scenery DATs (zone + 100, zone + 83191 from 600): 961 type-2 MMBs in 81 zones (67,397 type 1, 5
  type 0), e.g. zones 4, 7, 8, 102..125, 215, 250.

## Config tool 0030 "3D LCD Mode" (2026-10-29)

- Retail: FUN_1000ca70 (frame flag and counter), FUN_1000c360 (eye projections), FUN_1000b4f0 (side-by-side blit),
  FUN_1000afd0 (the strip); more at the end of this entry.
- Retail draws the 3D world twice, eye 0 through projection x Translate(-0.006, 0, 0) and eye 1 through +0.006: a
  constant NDC shift, no parallax by depth. So each eye is the same picture moved 0.3 % of the width; ours draws it
  once into a scene target 0.6 % wider (the aspect widened to match, same pixel scale) and crops it twice: eye 0 =
  the right-hand part, eye 1 = the left-hand part (only the 0.3 % margins beyond the plain frustum differ from a
  second render, and those are drawn too).
- render/scale.rs blit: eye 0 squeezed into the window's left half, eye 1 into the right, bilinear (retail then puts
  its composite to the window with point filtering; ours samples the scene once). The UI draws once over it
  *(inf, as retail)*.
- Counter 0..3 per frame (App::lcd_frame); on odd values the bottom 10 window rows get the 1 x 16 strip texture
  (row 0 black, rows 1..15 (0x48, 0, 0)): one black row, nine dark red, drawn opaque, under our UI *(inf: retail's
  blend and order for it)*.
- Not modelled: retail's unused 1024 x 2 magenta / green textures (made, never bound).
- Seen live: the gate in East Ronfaure side by side, the strip on frames 2 and 4 of four.

From the research notes:
- 0030 = DAT_10456abc (2019 DAT_104441a4), default 0. 2019 addresses unless marked cur.

## Config tool 0017 "Bump Mapping" (2026-10-29)

- Retail: FUN_10181b50 (the two-light model), FUN_10169d10 (the corner tangent); more at the end of this entry.
- On (read at the zone load, never in zone 182): the zone's bump DAT (dat/bump.rs: file 39831 + zone, 83991 + zone
  from 600) gives its Bp height maps, each made a normal map as FUN_1001d270 (wrapping neighbours; R from the rows
  above / below, G from the columns, B = 128 + 255 s) *(inf: the rows are taken as stored, no flip)*.
- A strip mesh (MMB header byte 4 = 1) whose every model texture has a bump map (name bytes 8..15 equal, trailing
  blanks ignored) becomes type 3: each triangle unrolled to its own corners, corner a's tangent from the triangle in
  drawn order (a, b, c): d = (Pc - Pb)(ua - ub) - (Pa - Pb)(uc - ub) normalised ((0, 0, 1) when zero), T = d x Na.
  Tangents share the deltas buffer (globals binding 4) with the sway deltas; vertex flags bit 1 tells them apart.
- Opaque type-3 draws go through scenery_bump / fs_bump (the normal map at group 2): vs_main's oD1 = 0.5 (T.L, B.L,
  N.L) + 0.5 with L toward the eased light (the area's when it has one); ps r1 = sat(t1_bx2 . v1_bx2), r1 x sat(diffuse
  x vc) + sat((ambient + points) x vc), x 2 x texture. Ours keeps the per-pixel point lights; cut-out and blended
  type-3 models draw the plain way *(not retail)*.
- The lighting model (FUN_10174610) follows the setting for all scenery: on, the one eased light and vertex fog over
  the eye range (RANGEFOG; ours interpolates the range and fogs per pixel); off, two lights not eased, the sun
  (E+0xa4, background sun colour E+0xe4) and the moon (E+0xc4, moon colour E+0xf4), both x the light scale (a flags-bit-0
  environment: its data direction with the sun colour, no second light), and table fog over the view depth.
  Lighting::two carries them; Uniforms / AreaGpu `two`, Uniforms `modes.x`.
- Settings' row takes effect at the next zone load (the meshes are built then; the lighting mode follows at once).
- Seen: zone-shot 230 (44 Bp, 41 used on 654 draws), on vs off differ over every directly lit face and the bumped
  walls; live East Ronfaure (20 normal maps on 225 draws) with no errors.

From the research notes:
- 0017 = DAT_10456bf0 (2019 DAT_104442d8), FFXiMain default 0 (ours 1). 2019 addresses unless marked cur.
- Enable: FUN_10171360 (cur FUN_10178250), run by FUN_10171c40 on the zone manager's first update (+0x34 == 0; once
  per process *(inf)*), sets zone +0x39498 (bump) and +0x3949c (light mode) only with 0017 != 0 and VS / PS 1.1
  (device +0x909 / +0x90a *(inf: the cap flags)*), and assembles five vs.1.1 shaders (0..4 point lights; sources
  0x1036af98 / 0x1036afe8 / 0x1036b070 / 0x1036b108 / 0x1036b1b0) and one ps.1.1 (0x1036b264). FUN_101720a0 copies the
  mode at each zone load, 0 in zone 182 (env +0x1b4 == 0xb6). 287 zones have a bump DAT with Bp chunks (1..103 each;
  FUN_10171f00, cur FUN_10178df0).
- Type 3: strips unrolled to lists (degenerates dropped, winding kept), 48-byte vertices pos, normal, colour, uv,
  tangent @0x24; model +0xbc = the bump texture. The Bp chunk: "bp\0\0", u16 width @4, u16 height @6, 8 zero bytes,
  name[16] @16, width x height 8-bit heights @32 (powers of two); FUN_1001d130 makes the texture. FUN_1001d270 (cur
  FUN_1001e0a0), with wrapping neighbours: gy = 2(prev[x] - next[x]) + prev[x-1] + prev[x+1] - next[x-1] - next[x+1],
  gx = 2(cur[x-1] - cur[x+1]) + prev[x-1] + next[x-1] - prev[x+1] - next[x+1], s = 127 / sqrt(gx^2 + gy^2 + 255^2),
  texel R trunc(gy s) + 128, G trunc(gx s) + 128, B 128 + trunc(255 s), A 0; category 0, so stored DXT3 when the
  device can *(inf)*.
- Draw (FUN_10175ac0 case 3): the vertex shader by point-light count (zone +0x3945c..+0x39468; positions into object
  space, colour = light +0x60 x colour, range^2 from light +0x4c), the pixel shader +0x39494, stage 0 the colour
  texture, stage 1 the bump, stride 0x30. VS: oFog = clamp((c9.z - w) c9.x, 0, c10.x); B = N x T; oT0 = oT1 = uv; oT2
  = c6 x vc; oT3 = c7 x vc plus per point light max(N.Lp / |Lp|^3, 0) masked by |Lp|^2 <= c18 through the colour
  matrix c15..c17, x vc. PS alpha = 4 v0.a t0.a. Mode 0 draws type 3 with FVF 0x152 and no shaders.
- Lighting (FUN_10174610): mode 1 (and 2) one directional light (FUN_10184980, the eased background light), light 5
  off, vertex fog (FOGVERTEXMODE LINEAR, TABLEMODE NONE, RANGEFOG when supported); mode 0 table fog when supported.

## Config tool 0022 "Opening Movie" (2026-10-29)

- Retail: FUN_10017a90 (CXiOpening update), FUN_102143b0 / FUN_10214470 (texture renderer), FUN_10213810 (the
  quad), FUN_102137b0 (stop); more at the end of this entry.
- `mov/mov999.pmv`: "PMUS", then an MPEG-1 video elementary stream XORed by file offset with `c2 ee 9c d9 bd 6c 4d
  72` (o % 8). Ours decodes it itself (mpeg1.rs: sequence headers and matrices, I / P / B pictures, slice and
  macroblock VLCs, dequantisation, float IDCT, half-pel motion; display order) on a thread: all 12,620 pictures in about
  20 s, 21x real time. A slice's macroblocks stop at the next start code, which is then left for the picture loop
  (reading past it there lost every other picture).
- Retail, per frame: state 0 opens the movie (DirectShow, polmvf.dll + the system MPEG-1 decoder); failure: done at
  once. With sound on, `mov/music999.bgw` (plain WAVE, id 0x400 in ours: audio/format.rs music_path) plays at 0x7f.
  State 1: any input (FUN_10007c70(0)) stops the movie (the object released: nothing drawn), fades the music over
  0x3c ticks and waits 0xf0 ticks (4 s) on black; the movie's end stops it and the opening is done at once (the
  music is not stopped). Ours takes any key or mouse-button press *(inf: the three counters FUN_10007c70 reads)*.
- The picture: the decoder's RGB24 samples are copied row by row into rows 0..335 of a 512 x 512 texture, and the
  quad (x 0..W, y from (off) k to (512 + off) k, k = H x 0.00214534, off -110 English / -160 subtitled) has v = 1 at
  its top corners, so the picture is the bottom 336 rows, upright: 0.142 H..0.862 H, the full width (a 1.85:1 band at
  4:3, stretched wider on wide windows, as retail) *(inf: the samples bottom-up, the decoder's usual RGB24)*.
  render/movie.rs: Y / Cb / Cr as R8 textures, BT.601 studio range in the shader, bilinear, on black; no gamma (retail
  sets a 1.0 ramp for it). Colour 0x80808080 taken as 1.0 *(inf)*.
- Ours (client/opening.rs, App::draw_opening): the movie clock starts with the music (status bgm = 0x401) or a
  second after the open; late pictures are dropped. The title's data and flyover load behind the movie; the opening
  ends when it is over and the title can draw. The window shows with the movie. English: no subtitles (the JP
  sprite file 39531 and the 24 frame windows at 0x10345cc8 not drawn).
- Settings' row takes effect on restart; default On (FFXiMain's). Test drives skip it unless FFXI_OPENING is set; their
  script then runs as phase "opening" (a key skips, shot: photographs). `movie-shot --frames N,.. --out DIR [--size
  WxH]` writes frames (CPU colour) or the window as drawn.
- Seen: a driven run, the movie with its music, Escape, 4.0 s of black, the title and its music; the GPU frames
  match the CPU conversion.

## Correction: the lobby scenes already blend in gamma space (2026-10-29)

- "The world scene blends in gamma space" ended with "Not yet: the title flyover, character select and creator
  scenes (still sRGB)". That was never true of the client: its surface has been Bgra8Unorm (plain) since the first
  commit (egui wants a non-sRGB target), and the scene target takes the surface's format, so every scene, the lobby's
  included, has been written and blended in gamma space. The sRGB target that cut the canal water was zone-shot's.
  The creator's dancer shader writes gamma values for a plain target (render/dancer.rs), which is what it gets.
- flash-shot rendered to Rgba8UnormSrgb, the last 3D tool doing so; now Rgba8Unorm like the client. char-shot's
  own single-model shader (render/character.rs) keeps its sRGB target: it draws one opaque model, no blending.

## Our upscale pack: undithered images lost their colour under alpha 0 (2026-10-29)

- User report: Lower Jeuno's floor around the Home Point drew black (decals over it fine). Not bump mapping (same
  with 0017 off), not the renderer (fine with the mods off): vana-upscale's `model   ground_1` (zone 245, file 345)
  had mean RGB 7 against stock 94, alpha mean 9 in both. The floor draws opaque, so the colour under alpha 0 shows.
- Cause: the undither step ("dithered glows and DXT3 banding") took it for a translucent glow (alpha dither 0.59,
  two thirds of its visible pixels partial); its premultiplied blur divided back to black where alpha is 0.
- Fixed in all 2,270 undithered images (~/ffxi/lab/scratch/checker/fix_rgb.py): colour from the plain upscale
  (upscale/up_dithered) where the undithered alpha is low, from the undithered one at alpha 48 and up, blended between;
  the alpha stays undithered. Their encodings dropped and 4,218 DATs rebuilt by tex-pack.
- Offscreen: Lower Jeuno's floor as stock (zone-shot 245 at 11:30 from (18, -6, 64)); zone 101's gate halo still smooth.

## Extras: Battle Text (short) and Battle Names (coloured) (2026-10-29; ours, Battlemod's simplify and colours)

- Two Extras rows, off by default: Battle Text Retail / Short (config `short_battle`), Battle Names Plain / Coloured
  (`battle_name_colours`). Both UIs.
- Names: dat::battle::Who.colour; the expander wraps the actor / target name (grammar kinds 0x10 / 0x11, code 1c 0 / 1)
  in `1e colour` .. `1e 01`, after any article. combat::name_colour for battle messages only (print): us and our pet
  7 (pale yellow), our party (trusts and pets in it) 6 (cyan), the alliance 3 (blue), a monster our party claimed 8
  (orange), anyone else's claim 5 (magenta), others the line's colour (table 0x103353c8, x2 as drawn). The condensed
  target lists keep each name's colour.
- Short (client/battlemod.rs): the message's retail lines read back with the actor's and target's printed forms ("The
  Wild Rabbit", "the Wild Rabbit", "Wild Rabbit") as tokens, then matched: "A hits T for N points of damage." / "A
  misses T." / "A uses X, but misses T." / "A uses X on T." on one line; "A uses / casts X." or "A scores a critical
  hit!" or "Skillchain: S." over a target line (takes N points of damage, recovers N HP / MP, gains / receives the
  effect of E, E effect wears off, N HP / MP drained, resists, no effect, evades, a Magic Burst! prefix); a target line
  alone. Out: "A [X] → T: R" (R: N, N! for a critical, miss, +N HP, +E, -E, resisted, ...), "T: R" alone. Anything else
  prints as retail. Short lines are not condensed (the modern chat's repeat fold still counts equal lines).
- `battle-dump [ids]`: every basic battle message's English text with sample names and its raw codes.
- Live (Lnxtest at a Snipper, modern UI): "Snipper → Lnxtest: 17", "Lnxtest → Snipper: miss (x2)", "32!" for a
  critical, the claimed Snipper orange; "uses Provoke on the Snipper" then added as a form.

## /sitchair: the chair under the sitter (2026-10-29)

- Ours had the seated pose and no chair. Now client/chair.rs: the chair is the sitter's second actor (id CHAIR 0x8000_0000 |
  sitter; retail entity +0xa4, kind status - 2), file 100507 + (status - 0x3f) (chairs 0..12 = statuses 0x3f..0x4b;
  13..20 have no file: no chair), for PCs only (ActIndex <= 0x6ff, no NpcPetFlag / Flags3 bit 25; FUN_1008f740).
- At the sitter's place and facing, untilted (FUN_100caf90); its own motion pick 'ci1' (its `ci10` is static); its
  `init` on load (invisible 4 ticks, fade in over 86); per-axis scale (Actor::axes; FUN_100cf210): height the sitter's
  size relative to medium, facing / side 1.0, Mithra 0.90 deep, Galka 1.20 deep with its side relative.
- The sitter: the chair motion files (tag 9, ride::motion_files(pc, 4)) while seated; `chi0` once they are in (state
  0x17 -> 0x18); wep0..8 hidden while seated (again after a model rebuild). A status leaving the chair starts the
  stand-up (state 0x19): `chi2` on the sitter and the chair (it fades out after 90 ticks), the weapons shown with wep2
  hidden, the new status held 186 ticks (chair::holding beside combat::held); then the chair goes and ours sends one
  more c2s 0x113 {2, 0} (LAB_1008c376). A chair -> chair change keeps the first chair (below). Shadows: our chair a
  silhouette, others' none; no bone-0 drop for the chair.
- /sitchair (FUN_1007c390): status gate 0x50 and SendResRdy; "on" 1 / "off" 2 / a number 0..20 as mode 0; nothing while
  sitting down, "on" while seated, "off" while standing. A toggle or "off" while seated starts our stand-up and is sent as
  {2, 0} *(not retail: retail sends {0, n}; LSB 0x113_sitchair.cpp takes a toggle with another chair id as a move to
  that chair, so "/sitchair" in chair 1 put us on the stool, seen live)*. The movement stand-up's "/sitchair off" now
  goes as mode 2 (it went as a toggle of chair 0 before).
- Live (Lnxcsfix, Mithra, East Ronfaure): `!addkeyitem 2826`, /sitchair 1 (the imperial chair fades in, chi0, seated
  on it), /sitchair (chi2 on both, standing, chair gone), /sitchair 0 (the stool), /sitchair off.
- LSB facts (not patched): chair 12's key item check uses 2837, the real one is 3343; its "sitting" checks stop at
  chair 10; the toggle-with-another-id case above. Others' chairs need a second player (not seen live).
- Not done: trusts ignoring chair / sit / heal statuses in 0x00E (asm 0x1009c148).

From the research notes:
- c2s 0x113 (size 0xc): u32 mode @4, u32 chair @8. LSB sets status 63 + n (the same status again stands) and wants
  key item 63 + n + 0xACA for chairs > 0.
- Chair status predicate FUN_10095790 (0x3f..0x53; actor side FUN_10084330). Kind = DAT_1035b3ec[applied status]
  (asm 0x10090cef), predicate vtable +0x36c = FUN_10082860 (0x3d..0x51). File: FUN_100d2f60's +0x36c branch,
  FUN_100c51c0(3, kind - 0x3d) -> FUN_100c5280 = n + 0x1889b, a self-contained model (FUN_100d0d70). A sitter race
  9..0x1c only logs an error and goes on.
- Chair files (all 13 alike): skeleton `chai` (3 bones, the root turned 90 degrees about Y, bone 2 at 0.507 up), one
  mesh, motions `idl0` / `ci10` (2 frames, no tracks: it never animates), schedulers `init` / `chi2`, info 0x45
  `00 00 00 ff ff ff 64 64 64 64 64 5a 87 78 ff ff` (leg mode 0: no ground tilt), a type-1 `sit_` chunk; no sounds,
  no generators.
- FUN_1008f740's first pass for an entity (+0x120 bit 9 clear) applies +0x16c directly, so a player already seated
  when it comes into range starts in the chair status. The chair is made (asm 0x10090ca9..0x10090d13) when the
  applied status is a chair, there is no second actor (+0x120 bit 10) and the sitter's model is loaded
  (FUN_100d12d0); gate FUN_1008e130 (ActIndex <= 0x6ff), +0x12c bit 30 (NpcPetFlag) and bit 31 (u32 @0x28 bit 25)
  clear; passing: FUN_100d2bc0(4), +0x120 bits 11..12 = 2 (chair type). A failed gate still builds an actor with a
  leftover kind and no type bits, deleted next frame *(inferred: it draws nothing)*. FUN_100c59b0 links the pair
  through +0x768; FUN_100c5d60 resets the per-axis scales +0x758 / +0x75c / +0x760 to -1.
- Deletion FUN_10092870 (also from FUN_10092900: despawn, zone-out, model rebuild): type 2 -> FUN_100d44b0(9) drops
  the tag-9 motion files; the chair deleted, both links and +0x400 cleared.
- FUN_100d0d70 -> FUN_100d0fc0: kinds 0x25..0x34 (vt +0x378, the Indi auras) and chairs (vt +0x36c) run their own
  `init` (vtable +0x298 on themselves). Chair `init` (length 90): op 0x29 colour 0 at once (advance 4), op 0x29 to
  0x80808080 over 86. The chair's `chi2` (length 168): op 0x01 wait 90, op 0x29 to 0x00808080 over 78.
- The sitter's chair motion files (FUN_100d2bc0(4), tag 9, the riding tables' slot 4; skipped for entity type +0xee
  2): Hume M / F 38607 / 38703, Elvaan M / F 38799 / 38895, Taru 38991, Mithra 39087, Galka 39183 (motions
  `ci00`..`ci21`, schedulers `chi0`..`chi2`); the skirt files (`ci02 ci12 ci22`) 32 and 64 past each.
- Names: FUN_1008a160's base +0x1a0 = 'ci1 '; FUN_1008a1a0 in a chair status sets the stand bases +0x1a4 / +0x1a8 /
  +0x1ac to 'ci1 ' when the gate passes, else 'si1 '. FUN_100c8bb0 picks 'ci1 ' (no gate) unless DAT_104568fc +9 is
  set and actor +0x79c (vt +0x200) clear *(inferred: an event pose flag)*.
- The machine (FUN_1008b460, state entity +0x1bc; FUN_1008e9a0 runs it each frame and keeps +0x170 while it returns
  0; it returns 0 at the top while the busy hold +0x11c is set):
  - state 0 with a chair applied: -> 0x17; ActIndex <= 0x6ff hides byte 0 of wep0..8 (FUN_100d60c0(0)).
  - 0x17: once FUN_100d12d0 (the chair files in): FUN_1008a1a0, then FUN_1008c450(0, gate failed) from
    "chi0sit0chi2sit2" (`chi0`, else `sit0`) -> 0x18.
  - 0x18: while the server status is a chair, return 1. A chair -> chair change is applied but the chair actor stays
    the first one: the type check tests only "a chair". Else -> 0x19 (zoning, FUN_10087060 = DAT_10487e48
    *(inferred)*: straight to the stand-up).
  - 0x19 (LAB_1008c2b5): `chi2` / `sit2` on the sitter; gate passed: `chi2` on a linked chair, FUN_100d5ef0(0) shows
    wep0..8, FUN_100d60e0(2, 0) hides wep2 -> 0x1a.
  - 0x1a (held 186 ticks by `chi2`'s op 0x1f): applied no longer a chair -> state 0; still a chair -> LAB_1008c376,
    return 1. LAB_1008c376 runs "/sitchair off" (0x1035bb04) for our own entity.
- Sitter schedulers (38607): `chi0` (312): op 0x1f busy hold d 230, 0x07 no reactions 230, 0x2e move lock 230, 0xb5
  no blink 200, op 0x05 `ci0?` 200, then `ci1?` 112. `chi2` (186): ops 0x1f / 0x2e / 0x07 d 186, op 0x05 `ci2?`
  186. `chi1` (`ci1?` 112) is named by no code.
- /sitchair's mode is FUN_10079170 ("on" 1, "off" 2, else 0 with chair = atoi, 0 outside 0..20; on / off send
  chair 0); mode 0 or 2 while seated in state 0x18 sets 0x19 locally and sends; in 0x19 / 0x1a only mode 2 is sent.
  In 0x19 with the server still seated LAB_1008c376 re-runs "/sitchair off" every frame until the status arrives
  *(the send queue may merge them; not traced)*; ours sends once. The movement stand-up is FUN_10157fa0 (config
  0x46).
- Placement (FUN_100c63d0 -> FUN_100caf90 each frame): the sitter's drawn base +0x5fc (before any +0x60c offset),
  rotation +0x61c, floor and lighting state (five 0x68-byte light blocks at +0x388), event scale (vt +0x204 ->
  +0x208) and +0xb2 bit 4 (the layout-mode hide) are copied to the chair; nothing is written to the sitter. The chair
  runs its own motion pick (FUN_100c83c0, 'ci1 '); the sitter's motion switches are not pushed to it.
- Scale (FUN_100cf210, asm 0x100cf599..0x100cf615): +0x754 = S.info[10 + GraphSize] / S.info[11] (S the sitter);
  k = FUN_10022170(race): Mithra 0, Galka 2, else none; +0x758 = chair.info[11 + k] / 100, +0x760 = chair.info[10 +
  k] / 100, 1.0 without k. Both bytes are read signed (MOVSX), so Galka's info[12] 0x87 is -1.21 and its side falls
  back to the relative size *(read from asm, not seen; looks like a retail bug)*. Draw (FUN_100cbde0 asm
  0x100cc6b4..0x100cc7f5): an event scale >= 0 wins on every axis, else each axis when >= 0, else +0x754; +0x75c is
  never set for a chair.
- A model made while seated hides wep0..8 by FUN_1008c480 instead of its `init`.
- The open trust item: an 0x00E entity with u8 @0x28 bit 0 (TrustFlag) ignores server statuses 0x21, 0x2f and
  0x3f..0x53 (+0x16c not written; asm 0x1009c148..0x1009c16d).
- Event binding (FUN_100bcdd0, FUN_100bd1a0): a bound PC-type entity (+0xee 0 / 2 / 6 / 7) gets event status 0 even
  seated; only +0xee 1 keeps 0x2f / chairs / 0x30 *(so a cutscene stands a seated PC up; not traced further)*. A
  model-id / costume switch (FUN_10095e90) waits while seated.
- *Inferred*: whether retail's other hides (+0xb2 bits 1 / 5) reach the chair (only bit 4 is copied); +0x12c bit
  31's meaning (LSB leaves Flags3 bit 25 unknown).

## zone-path: doors open or shut (2026-10-30; tool)

- `zone-path ZONE --from x,y,z --to x,z [--open-doors [--closed "x,z;x,z"]]`: --open-doors skips every door's collision
  box (Ground::open_doors_except) but those whose box centre is within 3 of a --closed point, and lists each door by id
  (its 4cc name, "_440" = 0x3034345f) with its box centre (Ground::door_boxes). So which door a route needs: it
  reaches with all open and fails with that one shut.
- Qulun Dome (148), for the LSB walkthrough: arrival A (337.9, 20.1) reaches the Quadav Crest ??? only through _441;
  the Magicite reaches arrival C (2.9, 60.0) only through _440 (from the Magicite out: its raised floor is not entered
  by this walk's 1.2 step); arrival B is a closed pocket (533 cells) even with every door open.

- `map-borders ZONE A B`: floor triangles (|normal y| > 0.6) of sub-map key A whose corners lie within 0.6 of key-B
  floor corners (Ground::key_borders), clustered within 8, each with its square on both maps; also each key's floor
  triangle count.

  both maps). zone-path from the Pashhow arrival reaches only the H-7 one.

## Modern UI: flyouts anywhere (2026-10-30; ours, not retail; client/modern/fly.rs)
- User request: flyouts pulled off their edge stand free in the middle; sliding one along its edge shows no ghost (only
  a drag well off it does); any window can be a flyout on a screen edge; any window can dock onto another's side as a
  flyout, the two frames joined (no border where they meet, the docked one's band curving into the other's).
- Holds (fly::Attach): Free, Edge (screen left / right, its top a fraction of the screen), Side (another panel's left
  or right, `along` points below its top). Saved in ModernPlace: `fly` (to "" = the screen) and `float` (an edge
  window let go free); the edge windows keep their old x / y encoding while on the edge.
- Dragging: a held window slides along its hold within PULL (64 pt) of it, the window itself (no ghost); pulled further,
  its ghost follows the pointer, or sits where it would be held, and it lands there when let go (a screen edge within
  10 pt, a panel's side within 28, else free). A free window moves live; near a hold its ghost shows the held place. The
  grab is taken at the press origin, so the window does not trail the pointer by egui's drag threshold.
- A panel's side takes a flyout only where it fits clear of its corners (flyout height + 2 x (24 + fillet 8) <= its
  height); the flyout's top is clamped there. What it rides not shown, it stands where it last stood.
- Frames (pack style; borders::fly, paint::window_cut / joint): a screen-edge flyout is the frame drawn 24 pt (the corner)
  past the edge, its band running into it. A joined pair: the panel's side band is left out over the joint (Cut.gaps),
  the flyout's frame is drawn 24 pt into the panel and clipped at the fillets (Cut.clip), both interiors on the panel's
  gradient span (Cut.grad), and a patch of that gradient fills between them; the fillets are quarter circles (r 8) from
  the panel's band middle (3 pt in: the band is 0.5 clear, dark 1.5, mid 0.5, bright 1, mid 0.5, dark 1.5) to the
  flyout's, stroked dark 5 / mid 2 / bright 1 in the frame's band colours (read from the frame image). The interior
  gradient now interpolates between the image's rows.
- Generic panels (Panels::show) held: fixed where the hold puts them, a background drag; on a screen edge a round knob
  on the inner side folds them into a tab (cfg.modern_folded "fly <id>"), the tab's click opens it. The edge windows
  (extras.rs) use the same holds, tabs and drags, now in the pack frame with the jewel on an edge.
- Live (Lnxcsfix, 2026-10-30): Wide Scan slid down its edge with no ghost; pulled into the middle (ghost), let go free;
  the Items window docked onto its right side joined, followed it, pulled to the screen's right edge (snap ghost),
  folded to a tab and back; Wide Scan back onto the left edge; the chat nudged stays free, the location panel on it.
  Not done: top / bottom joints.
- The frames differ only in their band (normal gold, focused blue, alert red; the interiors are the same rows), so the
  fillets run from the band the target was drawn in (Modern.frames, Open::Side.band) to the flyout's, blended by the
  angle round the arc (PathStroke::new_uv); a frameless target ("none": the status icons) takes no joint.

## Escha - Zi'Tah: Affi and the Register of Deeds (2026-10-30; read for the LSB session)
- User report: talking to Affi (17957449) or the Register of Deeds (17957450) in zone 288 did nothing, on the retail
  client too. LSB defines both in data/zones/escha_zitah/npcs.yaml but has no scripts for them, so the talk gets a
  bare release. Not ours: reported to the LSB session with the events below.
- Their events (event DAT 85023): Affi 9700 (first talk), 9701 (later talks), 9702..9704 (pick a key item); the
  Register 9708. The full read (start params, every server_update and the reply fields it reads, finish options,
  the key item shop with its fixed prices, the temporary item table) is below.
- VM facts confirmed on the way (event_vm.rs already does them): message `{num1..7}` are Z3..Z9 and `{num8}` up are
  G0 up (Affi's code table 0x27ba lists them); `table` sub 5 writes through such a table of register ids.
- Silt / bead lines in the zone dialogs (LSB ids = installed ids, msgshift delta 0): kill-style "You receive {num0}
  pinch[/es] of escha silt[ for a total of {num1}]." 288 7712 / 7713, 289 7831 / 7832, 291 7858 / 7859 (beads the next
  two); chest 7632 / 7751 / 7681 and Domain Invasion 7644-7645 / 7763-7764 / 7693-7694 ("You obtain", colour 0x79).
  No "can't hold more silt" line exists in any of them *(inf: retail caps silently)*.

From the research notes:
- The VM side: start num0..num7 land in Z2..Z9; each server_update (op 0x43: c2s 0x05B mode 1, option Z1) waits for a
  0x05C whose num0..num7 overwrite Z2..Z9 (an unanswered update hangs the event). Options pack command bits 0..7, sub
  8..15, count 16..31; a menu cancel finishes with 0x40000000. A menu hide mask's bit k hides option k. What starts
  9702..9704 is not in the script: the server picks the csid *(inf: a trade)*.

## Modern UI: flyouts anywhere taken out again; edge windows float; the skillchain helper reworked (2026-10-30)
- User: "I hate the new interface. Put it back the way it was" (making any window a flyout and joining windows'
  frames, "Modern UI: flyouts anywhere" and its two follow-ups). The modern UI files are back as they were at e6aa722;
  that code stays at tag `modern-ui-flyouts-anywhere`. Kept from the same request, as the user quoted only from its
  third point: edge windows (Timers, the map, Wide Scan, the training regime, the skillchain helper) slide along their
  edge with no ghost while within 64 pt of it, pulled further their ghost follows the pointer, and let go away from
  the edges they stand free (ModernPlace.float) with their whole frame; a free one moves with the pointer and lands
  on a screen edge it is let go within 10 pt of (or pushed past). Wide Scan under a free map stands free under it.
  Kept fixes: a bottom-placed panel (chat, party) dragged no longer creeps down (its bottom from its top plus its
  placed height); the drag is held where it was pressed.
- The skillchain helper (user: "half the information is cut off, and it's fairly useless"): skillchain::view builds
  what it shows (the open resonance on the focus monster with every closer, and every chain the party makes with all
  its ways); modern/extras.rs draws it 360 pt wide with every line wrapped (no ellipses), the closers as a column of
  chain and element icons beside who closes with what, each party chain with its two best ways (ours first, then
  those whose opener has the TP) and a click on its row for the rest; it scrolls instead of dropping lines when it
  runs into the next panel on its edge. `modern-shot --borders pack` draws a sample. Seen live with Naji and Ayame in
  South Gustaberg (nine chains, each way whole); the resonance part only in the sample (no chain made in that run).

## Modern chat: mouse selection, right-click copy, Ctrl+V into a closed line (ours, 2026-10-30)
- User: "Text in the chat window or chat input needs to be selecting and copyable via ctrl+c or right click. Ctrl + v
  should paste into chat input." Not retail (its log and line have no mouse selection; "Chat line: selection" above).
- modern/chatsel.rs. The lines: a drag selects from the press, each end a line's log index and a char of its text as
  drawn (timestamp included), so lines sliding in keep it; a wash behind the chars (galley rows); a click clears it.
  Ctrl+C: client/mod.rs's Copy takes the chat line's selection first, then the lines' (World::log_selection, set each
  frame), else it is /check as before. A right click on the lines opens Copy / Copy Line (the line under the pointer).
- The chat line: a press puts the caret at the nearest char boundary (a phrase is one unit), a drag selects
  (fep's chat_caret / chat_anchor, set after the frame); the selection now shows in the modern line too; a right click
  opens Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All. Paste reads the clipboard after the frame (egui_winit State::clipboard_text)
  and hands it back as a Paste event.
- Ctrl+V (egui-winit's Paste) with the line closed opens it with the text; with another text field taking typing
  (input_open) it goes there as before.
- The chat window holds (logwin rule `stacked`) while the pointer is over it or its menu is open: it folded away
  under the pointer while a line was aimed at (the drag then moved the window).
- The menu: the pack's window frame by the pointer, rows lit under it; a pick or a press elsewhere closes it.
- Script steps `copy` / `paste:TEXT` send egui-winit's Copy / Paste events; `rclick` now holds the button 50 ms (a
  press and release in one frame is no click to egui). The client logs "clipboard: copied N chars".
- Live (Lnxcsfix): a drag over three lines selected and Copy took 117 chars; Copy Line 62; in the line, a drag
  selected "orld", a paste replaced it, Select All and Copy took 11, the menu's Paste put the clipboard's "from the
  menu" in; Ctrl+V with the line closed opened it with the text. A driven window cannot set the Wayland clipboard
  (no real input serial), so the copies were checked by the log, the menu's paste by a clipboard set with wl-copy.
- Also: the skillchain helper's height no longer follows the room down to the panel under it (it grew and shrank as
  it slid); it scrolls past 60% of the screen's height. Edge windows are kept whole on the screen by their own height.
  Seen live: four heights along the right edge, the same window each time.

## The modern UI's widget kit and one key model (ours, 2026-10-30)
- User: "explain to me why we're not creating reusable widgets in the UI so that similar elements are guaranteed to
  behave the same way?", then "build the widget kit". The pages each drew and keyed their own rows, sliders, lists and
  frames, so like controls behaved differently (sliders needing Enter on one page only, lists not following the
  cursor, hover moving the cursor on some pages, four button copies, eight yes / no copies).
- modern/kit.rs. A page lists its stops top to bottom: Tabs (Left / Right turn them, Tab / Shift+Tab from anywhere on
  the page), Value (options as buttons, a toggle or a slider: Left / Right change it at once, Enter steps an option;
  options off are passed over), Buttons (Left / Right along the row, Enter presses, one off refuses with 0004), List
  (Up / Down walk it and leave at its ends, Left / Right or Page Up / Down a page, Home / End). Up / Down go round the
  stops; a list's last row's Down goes to the stop after it; a row of buttons keeps its column only from another row
  of buttons. `kit::key(stops, &mut at, key, shift)` returns Moved / Set / Press / Refused / Back.
- The widgets: button (one look: lit, off, the cursor's ring), setting (heading over its control, ringed and kept in
  view when the cursor comes to it), line (label left, control right), choice, buttons, slider (click or drag),
  tab_strip (tabs.rs's look with the cursor), list (scroll area, row faces, follow), scroll (the bar shown whenever
  the content is longer), yes_no, chevrons (stacked up / down), colour_picker (sRGB hue / saturation / value square
  and strip), field / caret_text, frame / inset.
- The mouse everywhere in the modern layer: hovering only lights a control (41 places moved the cursor on hover; all
  gone, the command and battle menus, the lobby rows, the prompts, the lists, the 2FA window's buttons too); a click
  puts the cursor there and takes it (the magic, ability, item and equipment lists took two clicks once hover no longer
  pre-selected).
- egui's scroll bars are solid (8 px, the pack's bronze on charcoal): its default floating bars were hidden until
  hovered, so long lists looked like they had none.
- On the kit: the Config pages (native pages, Chat Filters / Effects, Font Colors, Extras, Settings, Mods; the title's
  Config too), the magic and ability lists' sort strip (a row of buttons above the rows: Up from the first row, retail
  reaches it only by Num+), the macro palettes (the sets a tab strip, Tab turns them; Copy / Paste / Delete a row under
  the keys) and editor (Prev / Next, title and lines, then Copy / Paste / Delete Line: Tab, as retail's Num+, or Down
  from the last line), the comyn prompt, the "Sort them now?" question.
- Config: the key assignment pages (k1assign / k2assign) and Misc. 2's "Reset keyboard assignment to default?" are the
  page's own now (a list with each function's key, a key pressed assigns; the kit's yes / no), not retail's windows
  over it. Font Colors: a colour row opens a picker with Hue / Saturation / Brightness sliders; the picker shows the
  colours as they show on screen (a config channel of 0x80 is full: shown = 2 x value, capped).
- Settings > Mods: each pack ON / OFF, up / down chevrons, Uninstall (asks; deletes the pack's folder under the mods
  folder off the UI thread), Install from File at the top (a folder and archive picker from Downloads; zip, 7z, rar;
  read and unpacked off the UI thread), the archives found in Downloads under it as before.
- Character select (ours): the Settings button is a stop under the list (Down from the last character, Up from the
  first) and stays shown while its options are open; Escape on the select prompts is No in the modern layer (retail's
  ptc6yesn ignores it); the log-in prompt is the kit's, larger.
- The retail windows still drawn in the modern layer (the conquest, Besieged and Colonization maps' windows ...) get
  the modern frame at the panels' size (its corner 24 egui points in UI pixels: GameUi::modern_scale), standing out
  past the window by its border and a margin (render/ui.rs push_modern_frame); the map's info windows keep that far
  in from the screen's edges.
- The command menu in the Mog House: retail's row 12 is Mog House there (FUN_1013ff90); it is a row of its own, and the
  map's category keeps Region Info and Current Time.
- Also: the 2FA recovery code has a Copy button (and Ctrl+C); the weather icon is centred in the whole location panel;
  the compass's tracked target is larger and pulses; macro keys are plain (no corner ornaments) with their number in
  white at the top right.

## Footsteps: the model file's folder, not the 'foot' tone (2026-10-30)

- User: a "telegraph beep" from Heraldic Imps (and Puks, other flyers) from the moment they came near; retail plays
  their wing beats at the same cadence. Heraldic Imp, model 52021: Cib (3, 35, 0) = leg mode 3 (steps also while
  standing), footstep kind 35 'z'. Its `0Nz1` SeSeps (se 147001 in fses, 147002 in fser) and `0az1` (127003 / 127004)
  sit in the model file; Caedarva Mire's zone DAT 179 has no 'z' steps. Live (Lnxcsfix by an Imp, footsteps logged):
  a step every 200..250 ms, about one gap in five under 150 ms.
- FUN_100d2970's sound lookup (section "Footsteps"): a name missing from the actor's folder (+0x800, the zone's fses /
  fser) switches it to the same folder in the actor's model resource (vtable +0x1e0 = actor+0xb4) and searches again;
  that folder stays the actor's (+0x800, its 4cc at +0x804) until the set changes; only a name missing there too
  falls to DAT 0's 'foot' = se 12, a 0.15 s 1047 Hz tone (retail logs "足音リソースの検索に失敗しました。" then).
  Ours searched only the zone's folder and played se 12 for every such step: the beep.
- Ours now (fx/mod.rs footstep, Foot, foot_set): the per-actor folder, the model file's (Character.files[0]) on a miss,
  the dust from that folder; the wading ripple's `i900` and op 0x78's fall thud read it too; cleared with the zone. A
  model file still loading plays no step rather than the tone. Test fx::tasks::tests::flyer_wing_beats.

## An actor's deletion takes its clones and tasks; fx-soak (2026-10-30)

- User report: the frame rate fell to about 40 fps after a while in Garlaige Citadel; F12 showed fx draw at 14.5 of
  17.8 ms, 1,095 live elements. The log's "effects live" line had 12 copies of each of model 52742's (model id 2447)
  generators (2063, 2185, dis0, lit0, lit1, pou0..pou4, ras0/1, sin0/1, tub0/1, uz00): that monster had despawned
  and come back 11 times, each new entity running `init` -> `mse0` -> (sub-animation 1) `ids1` -> `efon`, which
  stops its generators on the actor pair (`efkl`, op 0x1e) and starts them again with op 0x02 (endless 0x1000
  clones). The old sets had lost their actor, so `efkl` no longer matched them, and they ran on.
- Retail deletes them with the actor. CXiSkeletonActor's destructor (vtable 0x10330f40, FUN_100c5540 ->
  FUN_100c5c00) kills its held dust (+0x764) and `fvib` (+0x814) clones with FUN_100543a0, then FUN_10082b10 walks
  the caster (+0x68) and target (+0x6c) links calling each link's vtable +0x10 / +0x14:
  - CMoGeneratorClone (constructor FUN_100536c0, vtable 0x1032b69c, link sub-object +0x30 vtable 0x1032b680):
    FUN_10054380 / FUN_10054390 -> FUN_100543a0 (ADD ECX,-0x30; CALL; MOV AL,1): its elements deleted at once
    (FUN_100538e0(0), no burst), unlinked from both actors, the refcount forced to 0 and the clone freed.
  - CMoSchedularTask (vtable 0x1032b860, link +0x34 vtable 0x1032b844): FUN_10057cf0 / FUN_10057d10 delete the task
    (vtable +0x18(1)).
  - The base generator (CMoGenerator, vtables 0x1032b114 / 0x1032b140: FUN_10049290 / FUN_100492a0) only unlinks and
    returns 0: a generator run as its own template runs on, at the identity.
  - Both kinds of clone are linked: model-load clones (FUN_10085060, the actor as caster) and op 0x02's (FUN_10057fb0
    asm 0x10059afc, the task pair); element sub-clones (FUN_1004e8d0) inherit their parent's pair. FUN_100496f0
    never ends an endless clone by itself (it returns 1 only when the duration +0xd0 is set and reached).
  - Nothing else in the despawn path FUN_10092900 runs `efof` / `efkl` / `dead` *(found by a research pass over
    FUN_10092870 / 10092800 / 10092760 / 10092710 / 100926c0)*.
- Ours: Effects::forget_actor deletes the tasks with the actor as actor1 or actor2 and the instances linked to it that
  are clones (op 0x02's, the model file's), footstep dust / prints / the wading ripple (Owner::Step) or an element's
  sub-clones (driven); the others forget it as before. Its wading and footstep-folder entries go too. Test
  fx::tasks::tests::despawn_takes_clones (model 52742 in sub-animation 1, three spawns: none left; without the fix
  16 left after each).
- `vana-client fx-soak --out FILE [--model ID] [--cycles 3] [--ticks 300] [--settle 600]`: every 0x00E model id, on a
  stand-in actor in sub-animations 0 and 1: `init` and its model generators run, the actor despawns, `--cycles`
  times; a row for every model with effects left after a despawn (marked template / endless) or a spawn starting more
  than the one before. Without the fix it flags model 2447 (16, 32, 48 started).
- fx-soak's first full run (with the fix) still flagged 180 of 6314 model runs, all bursts: model 298 (file 1598)
  `st00` runs op 0x3f tm10 -> tm11, tm00 -> tm01, gp00 -> gp01 (B static, op 1 life 0). Retail (FUN_10057fb0):
  - op 0x3f with an attached A (asm 0x10059f98..0x1005a027): C = a new clone of B (FUN_100536c0(B, 0, 0, 1)),
    linked to the task's actor1 / actor2 when B is attached (+0x64 = the task); FUN_10053a00(A, pair, C) runs
    FUN_100538e0(A clone, C) on each A clone on the pair: per live A element C's count is reset (FUN_10053370), one
    emission with the A element as parent (FUN_100496f0), the A element deleted, then C soft-stopped (FUN_10053890).
    With no A clone a static B emits once and C is deleted (FUN_100543a0): nothing. An unattached static A morphs as
    its template into B's (asm 0x10059f66..0x10059f86).
  - end-stream op 1 (FUN_1004e720, asm 0x1004e7e6..0x1004e868) runs the resource itself: a static one's live elements
    are deleted first (FUN_100538e0(G, 0)), then the reset, one emission, the soft stop: one burst element per
    template at most. Emission op 0x3c (asm 0x1004ee0e..0x1004ee36) only zeroes +0xcc: a static one emits once per
    start (it emits only while +0x9c, the count since its start, is 0: asm 0x1004a605..0x1004a623).
  - A static element (max life 0) never ages and is never deleted by its generator handle going; elements have no
    actor links (FUN_10044970).
  Ours had given each burst its own instance (an endless element each). Now: op 0x3f as above; bursts run on the
  generator's one template instance (Effects::template_inst), op 1 clearing a static one's elements first; an
  unattached static generator started by op 0x02 restarts its running template (FUN_100531d0, Effects::restart;
  asm 0x100599e5..0x10059a39 links the template to the pair and restarts it) instead of a second instance.
  fx-soak then: 0 of 6314 runs leave anything (growth = a rise on every spawn; random emissions wobble).

## Windows: monitors of different scale, the modern UI's size, two debug-build panics (2026-10-31)

Tested on a real Windows 11 PC (DeepThought: DISPLAY1 2880x1800 at 200%, DISPLAY2 1920x1080 at 150%, DISPLAY12 and
DISPLAY13 at 100%; RX 6800 XT eGPU), MinGW cross builds, release and debug.

- The two crashes the user saw (2026-10-28) were egui `debug_assert!`s, so only debug builds (`cargo build` /
  `cargo run`) hit them; release builds never did:
  - "Texture modern/atlases/status_0@2x.png has size 2184x1776, but the maximum texture side is 2048": egui-winit
    passes the device's texture limit in its first RawInput only (`State::new(.., max_texture_side)`, taken by
    `RawInput::take`). The opening movie's frames take that input and drop it (logged on the box: "dropped by the
    opening"); egui then keeps its 2048 default. Ours now sets `raw.max_texture_side` every frame.
  - "Negative child size: [2346.4 -0.2]" on entering the world (Play): the modern chat window rounds its eased
    height to whole pixels, which with almost no rows fell a fraction under the chrome; the line area is clamped
    to 0 (and the kit slider's width too).
- winit 0.30.13 on Windows (event_loop.rs WM_DPICHANGED, runner.rs BufferedEvent):
  - It never answers WM_GETDPISCALEDSIZE, so Windows scales a dragged window linearly (its drag rectangle) and
    overrides the size ScaleFactorChanged asked for (1280x720 came out 637x357 from 200% to 100%). Ours subclasses
    the window (client/windpi.rs, SetWindowSubclass) and answers with the client size as it is plus the frame at the
    new DPI (AdjustWindowRectExForDpi; none for a borderless window).
  - During a drag it nudges the window back onto the monitor it is still mostly on, and the scale flipped back and
    forth (nine changes 100% <-> 150% in half a second, the window no longer following the pointer). Inside the
    move / size loop (WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE .. WM_EXITSIZEMOVE) ours puts the window at the rect Windows suggests after
    winit's handling, and at the loop's end restores the client size it began with if the scale changed.
  - A DPI change raised inside our own handler (set_outer_position for the Config Monitor row, the start-up
    with_position) is buffered: winit reads the size writer at once (the linear size), SetWindowPos's that, and
    replays ScaleFactorChanged later with a fresh writer whose value it then applies. The Resized for the linear
    size is queued after it and arrived last: the surface took 1920x1080 while the window was 1280x720 (egui then
    drew only the top-left 1280x720 of the frame). Resized now takes `window.inner_size()`, not the event's.
  - ScaleFactorChanged keeps the configured resolution (the first-start window's size during first start), not
    the surface's, which by then can already be the changed one; nothing in full screen.
  - set_fullscreen(None) restores the window's placement on its old monitor, rescaled by DPI (2570 wide came back
    5140): moving a window to another monitor leaves full screen first, then moves it over a few frames later.
- A windowed start passed no position, so Windows opened it on the primary monitor whatever the Monitor row said
  (the user's "snaps back to the first one"): it now opens centred on the configured monitor.
- The modern UI ignored the monitor's scale: `zoom = (height / native) / 1080 * size` cancelled egui's native
  pixels per point. It is now `height / 1080 * size` and egui multiplies the scale in, so a 200% panel draws it twice
  as large (the user: the login form was too small to fill in on a 13-inch 200% panel). egui-winit stamps
  `window.scale_factor()` into every frame's input, so the size follows the window to another monitor. The login
  form, laid out on game-UI rects (its mouse on the same rects), grows by the scale too, up to 0.4 of the UI height,
  its top kept below the logo's "ONLINE" line. Monitors at 100% (the Linux desktop here) see no change.

## Our upscale pack: the slim copy for publishing (2026-10-31)

- tex-pack writes whole game files: each packed DAT is the stock file with its images swapped, every other chunk
  (models, motions, the rest) copied from SE's file. The overlay (dat/overlay.rs merge) only ever takes D3s / Msb / Bp
  chunks from a mod, keyed by folder path, 4cc, kind, the texture's name and the n-th such chunk.
- `vana-client tex-slim --pack DIR --out DIR` (texpack::slim, dat::overlay::slim) keeps, per file, the folder markers
  (kinds 0 and 1: 16 and 32 bytes) and the D3s chunks that differ from the stock file's of the same key, and checks
  that the slim copy merges to the same bytes as the full one. mods/vana-upscale (30261006_0): 35,132 files, 27.5 GB
  full, 22.6 GB slim, none failed; the slim files hold only our images and the markers (0.4 MB of them in a tenth).
  Test dat::overlay::tests::slim_merges_the_same.
- LZMA (7z -mx=5) takes the upscaled DXT images to about a quarter (1.89 GiB of files to 0.42 GiB), so the published
  pack fits GitHub's 2 GiB per-asset limit in a few parts. Each part installs on its own from Settings > Mods (one
  Mods entry per part; their files don't overlap). `vana-client mod-install --archive FILE --root DIR` runs the Mods
  page's install (modpack::pack_of + install) into another folder, to check a part before publishing it.
- Published as its own GitHub release, created with `--latest=false`: the in-app Update reads /releases/latest.

## Motion loops: the frame count is the keys less one (2026-10-31)

- User report: running motions jerk very slightly at the point where they loop, "almost like it's missing a single
  frame" (the right elbow from behind, the feet looking down).
- The motion chunk (0x2B) header is u8 version, u8 converted, u16 tracks, u16 keys, f32 speed; each keyed channel
  holds `keys` floats (the blocks sit exactly `keys` apart). In the run and walk cycles the last key repeats the
  first (Hume, Mithra and Tarutaru race files: |last - first| = 0).
- FUN_10018900, the motion resource's loader ("Mo2 Version Error"), decrements the count at +0x34 by one while the
  converted byte (+0x31) is 0, then sets that byte: every motion chunk checked (3,776) has it 0. The player
  (FUN_10019ab0) wraps the frame at that count (or a positive override at +0x38; the start paths seen pass 0), and
  the key fetch (FUN_10018d00) reads keys floor(f) and floor(f) + 1 with no clamp. So a cycle of n keys loops over
  n - 1 intervals, its last one running into the closing key.
- Ours kept the key count as the frame count and wrapped at it, clamping to the last key: the closing key (equal to
  key 0) held for one whole interval at every loop, 4 ticks (67 ms) of a still pose per run cycle at rate 1.
- Now dat::character::parse_animation stores the frame count as the game does (keys - 1 while the converted byte is
  0) and still reads `keys` floats per channel; motion::loop_frame wraps at it without a clamp; one-shots end and
  hold at frame `frames` (the last key); motion lengths (frames / (speed x 0.5)) are one frame shorter, as retail's.
  Test motion::loop_tests::run_cycle_has_no_hitch (Mithra run0: every 60 Hz step moves the pose; it fails on the
  old wrap with "held pose at frame 12").

## Casting right after stopping: the position goes first (ours, not retail) (2026-10-31)

- User report: stopping and at once casting (Utsusemi), shooting or using an item is interrupted over and over,
  as though the server saw movement after the action started. Retail has the same behaviour (the user: "a bug we
  copied from retail").
- The client sends one datagram every 400 ms (retail's cadence), the queued commands first and the tick's 0x015
  last. LSB (magic_state.cpp, range_state.cpp, item_state.cpp) starts an action at the position it last heard
  (m_startPos = loc.p) and interrupts on any later 0x015 more than 0.3 away (items: changed at 0.1 rounding), and a
  cast at once when the last two 0x015 were more than 0.3 apart (m_startedMoving from m_lastMoveDistance, computed
  on every 0x015, moved or not). LSB's parse (map_networking.cpp) runs every sub-packet of a datagram whose sync is
  that datagram's, in order, and only then moves client_packet_id. So [cast, 0x015] started the cast up to 400 ms
  back on the run, then moved us: interrupted.
- Ours: when the datagram holds a 0x01A magic (category 3) or ranged attack (0x10), or a 0x037 item use, and we are
  not moving, the tick's 0x015 goes first and twice (client/net.rs add_position): the first moves the server to
  where we stopped, the second leaves m_lastMoveDistance 0, then the action starts there. Moving, the 0x015 goes
  last as before, so casting on the run is still interrupted.
- Live (Lnxcsfix as WHM 30, run 1.2 s, stop, cast at once; `act:autorun`, a test-only script step): old order 6 of 6
  Cures interrupted, new 6 of 6 cast; Potions 4 of 4 "fails to activate" against 4 of 4 used; casting while still
  running interrupted 2 of 2. Ranged attacks not tried live (same path). Test client::net::tests::position_before_
  interruptible_actions.
